policy: Translate only Description (zh). Never change Name / EnumValue keys.

Accumulator.en: Accumulates specific map types such as Water, Forest, or Snow from all available nodes.
Accumulator.zh: 从场景中可用节点累积特定类型的图，例如水、森林或雪。

SnowMask.en: Accumulate all snow as a flat mask.

SnowDepth.en: Accumulate all Snow Depth at absolute values.

WaterMask.en: Accumulate all water as a flat mask.

WaterDepth.en: Accumulate all Water Depth in absolute values.

DebrisColor.en: Accumulate just the DebrisColor (using Max mode).

Trees.en: Accumulate all trees generated by Trees and Shrubs nodes.

TreeDeadZones.en: Accumulate all dead zones in Trees nodes.

TreeFreshwater.en: Accumulate all fresh water flows from Tree nodes.

Restrict to Group.en: Restricts accumulating from other nodes that are in the same Group as the Accumulator node.

Adjust.en: The Fx node makes that process easier by combining all the common adjustments inside a single node and allowing you to toggle them on and off.
Adjust.zh: 将常用高度/数值调整集中在一个节点中，并可单独开关各项处理（又称 Fx）。

Multiply.en: Multiplies each value by a specified factor.
Multiply.zh: 将每个值乘以指定系数。

Shaper.en: Applies a shaping function to modify the curve of values.
Shaper.zh: 用塑形函数改变数值曲线。

Clamp.en: Restricts values to a specified minimum and maximum range.
Clamp.zh: 将数值限制在指定最小/最大范围。

Clip.en: Limits values by cutting off those outside a given range.
Clip.zh: 裁切超出给定范围的数值。

Drop.en: Removes values below or above a certain threshold.
Drop.zh: 按阈值丢弃偏低或偏高的值。

Autolevel.en: Automatically adjusts values to span the full output range.
Autolevel.zh: 自动拉伸数值以占满可用输出范围。

Equalize.en: Redistributes values to achieve a more uniform distribution.

Strong.en: Enhances the contrast or intensity of values.

Invert.en: Flips values to their opposite within the range.

Anastomosis.en: Anastomosis creates interconnected water flow based extractions, ranging from small pits to large river channels. It is useful for both terrains and textures.
Anastomosis.zh: 模拟辫状/网状水系连通结构。

Impact.en: The intensity of the process. Higher values create stronger physical impacts within the erosion process.

Width.en: Controls the horizontal spread of the anastomosis effect. Larger values produce wider channels and features.

Depth.en: Determines the vertical extent of the erosion. Higher values result in deeper cuts and more pronounced terrain features.

Downcutting.en: Specifies the style and aggressiveness of vertical erosion. Select from various modes to control how the terrain is carved downward.

Destructive.en: Applies aggressive downcutting, rapidly eroding and deepening channels.

Pits.en: Focuses erosion into localized depressions, creating pit-like features.

Flows.en: Simulates water flow erosion, carving smooth, continuous channels.

Rivers.en: Emphasizes river-like downcutting, forming distinct riverbeds.

Riversx2.en: Doubles the intensity of river downcutting for deeper, more defined riverbeds.

Riversx4.en: Quadruples the river downcutting effect, producing extremely deep and prominent river channels.

Flooding.en: Simulates broad, shallow erosion typical of flooding events.

Floodingx2.en: Doubles the flooding effect, increasing the area and depth of flood erosion.

Flooding_x4.en: Quadruples the flooding effect, creating extensive and deep flood-eroded regions.

Quality.en: Sets the processing resolution for the node. Higher quality yields more detailed results at the cost of performance.

Quarter.en: Processes at 1/4 resolution for fastest performance and lowest detail.

Third.en: Processes at 1/3 resolution, balancing speed and detail.

Half.en: Processes at 1/2 resolution for moderate detail and performance.

Full.en: Processes at full resolution for maximum detail and slower performance.

Smooth Edges.en: Softens the edges of eroded features, reducing sharp transitions and creating a more natural appearance.

Angle.en: Angle creates a selection mask covering all areas of the heightfield facing the specified range.
Angle.zh: 按朝向/角度条件生成遮罩或影响。

Azimuth.en: The direction from which to start the selection.

Falloff.en: The soft falloff at the maximum angle.

AO.en: Creates an ambient occlusion map that darkens recessed areas and enhances terrain depth.
AO.zh: 环境光遮蔽（Ambient Occlusion），增强凹处阴影感。

Quality.en: Sets the processing resolution for the ambient occlusion calculation. Higher quality provides more accurate and detailed results, but may increase computation time.

Low.en: Fastest processing with minimal detail. Suitable for previews or low-fidelity outputs.

Medium.en: Balanced processing speed and detail. Recommended for general use.

High.en: High detail with slower processing. Use when fine ambient occlusion is required.

Ultra.en: Maximum detail and accuracy. Best for final renders, but slowest to compute.

Enhance.en: Boosts the strength and clarity of the ambient occlusion effect, making shadows and depth more pronounced in the terrain.

Aperture.en: Aperture expands or compacts every feature on the terrain, similar to a camera's bokeh.
Aperture.zh: 光圈/开口相关控制，用于局部通行或造型。

Information.en: Displays additional information or metadata about the aperture operation and its current settings.

Mode.en: Specifies the morphological operation to apply to the input, affecting how features are expanded or contracted.

Dilation.en: Expands or grows features in the input by the specified shape and size, filling small holes and connecting nearby elements.

Erosion.en: Contracts or shrinks features in the input by the specified shape and size, removing small details and separating connected elements.

Size.en: Sets the size of the structuring element (aperture) used for the operation. Larger values increase the effect's reach.

Shape.en: Determines the geometric shape of the structuring element used for dilation or erosion, affecting the style of the transformation.

Disk.en: Uses a circular (disk-shaped) structuring element for smooth, rounded transformations.

Polygon.en: Uses a regular polygon as the structuring element, allowing for custom-sided shapes.

Asterisk.en: Uses a star or asterisk-shaped structuring element, emphasizing cross-like or radiating effects.

Line.en: Uses a straight line as the structuring element, applying the effect directionally.

Corner.en: Uses a corner-shaped structuring element, targeting angular or edge features.

Vertices Count.en: For polygon shapes, sets the number of vertices (sides) used, controlling the regularity and appearance of the structuring element.

Corner Angle.en: Specifies the angle of the corner for the 'Corner' shape, adjusting the sharpness or openness of the structuring element.

Direction.en: Sets the orientation or direction for directional shapes (such as Line or Asterisk), controlling the angle of the effect.

Antialiased.en: If enabled, applies antialiasing to the aperture operation, smoothing the edges of the transformed features for a cleaner result.

Autolevel.en: Automatically remaps the input to use the full available height or mask range.
Autolevel.zh: 自动将输入重映射，以占满可用的高度或遮罩范围。

BlobRemover.en: BlobRemover can remove smaller fragments or blobs near larger shapes. This is very useful for cleanup.
BlobRemover.zh: 移除孤立斑块/碎块，清理遮罩或地形噪点。

Range.en: Controls the sensitivity of the blob detection. Higher values detect a wider range of blob sizes or intensities.

Connectivity.en: Specifies how connected blobs must be to be considered a single shape. Higher connectivity allows blobs to be more loosely attached to larger shapes.

Enforce Quantization.en: If enabled, forces the use of quantization during blob detection, improving efficiency and consistency in identifying blobs.

Quantization.en: Sets the quantization level for blob detection, with values between 1 and 128. Lower values provide finer detail, while higher values group similar values together for faster and more efficient blob identification.

Blur.en: Blur diffuses sharp shapes and softens the terrain.
Blur.zh: Blur 扩散锐利形状并软化地形。

Bomber.en: Bomber takes an input heightfield and "stamps" or bombs it across the entire terrain surface using the randomization properties you set.
Bomber.zh: 在地形上散布/“轰炸”放置多种细节或实例效果。

Iterations.en: Number of instances the bombing operation will create. Higher values increase the number of scattered elements.

Multiplier.en: Quickly multiply the number of bombed instances by increasing or decreasing this value, scaling the overall density.

Size.en: The minimum and maximum relative size of bombed instances, allowing for variation in the scale of each element.

Size Distribution.en: Controls the uniformity of the size of bombed instances. Higher values produce more consistent sizes, while lower values allow greater variation.

Rotation.en: The minimum and maximum range of rotations for the bombed instances, introducing random orientation for each element.

Proportional.en: Determines whether instances should maintain height-to-size proportion. When enabled, scaling an instance will also scale its height proportionally.

Variable Height.en: Allows variations in the height of bombed instances, introducing additional randomness to their elevation.

Height.en: The minimum and maximum range of height variations for the bombed instances, controlling how tall or flat each element can be.

Distribution.en: The method used to distribute bombed instances across the surface.

Random.en: A randomized distribution that results in pure chaotic patterns, scattering instances unpredictably.

Grid.en: A normalized grid distribution function that results in a systematic, evenly spaced pattern.

Jitter.en: The random offset applied to each instance while distributing, adding natural variation to their placement.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different distribution patterns.

Fade Edges.en: Softens the edges of bombed instances, blending them more smoothly into the base terrain.

Blend Mode.en: Specifies how the base terrain and bombed instances are merged together.

None.en: Each instance overwrites the underlying terrain at its location.

Blend.en: Blends instances with the base terrain using standard blending.

Add.en: Adds the height values of instances on top of the base terrain.

Subtract.en: Subtracts each instance from the base and previous instances, creating depressions.

Difference.en: Creates a difference between the base and each bombed instance, emphasizing changes.

Multiply.en: Multiplies the base terrain with each bombed instance, modulating the result.

Screen.en: Adds the two inputs without overexposing the output, resulting in a lighter blend.

Max.en: Retains the maximum height values of each bombed instance and the base terrain.

Min.en: Retains the minimum height values of each bombed instance and the base terrain.

Quality.en: The level of quality to be used for the bombing operation. Draft is recommended for high-resolution previews, while Medium and High provide better final results.

Draft.en: Fastest processing with lower quality, suitable for previews.

Medium.en: Balanced quality and performance for general use.

High.en: Highest quality with the most detail, recommended for final output.

Add Input.en: Allows an additional input to be included in the bombing operation, enabling more complex or layered effects.

Bulbous.en: Bulbous inflates existing shapes to make them more voluminous while respecting standard geological boundaries.
Bulbous.zh: 生成圆鼓、块状的岩石/地貌体量。

Canyon.en: Canyon is a simple, fast, and detailed canyon primitive. It creates a drainage based river canyon.
Canyon.zh: 快速且细致的峡谷基础体：基于排水生成河谷型峡谷。

Structure.en: Selects the canyon shaping model used to generate the canyon form and surface character.
Structure.zh: 峡谷造型模型，影响形态与壁面特征。

Style.en: Selects the canyon shaping model used to generate the canyon form and surface character.
Style.zh: 峡谷造型模型，影响形态与壁面特征。

Classic.en: Clean, procedural canyon cuts with a simple, carved profile.
Classic.zh: 干净、程序化的切削剖面。

Eroded.en: Adds erosion-like breakup and natural irregularities to the canyon walls and floor.
Eroded.zh: 增加侵蚀破碎与自然不规则感。

Eroded2.en: A more advanced eroded style with richer wall detail and more natural variation.
Eroded2.zh: 更丰富的壁面细节与侵蚀感。

Strata.en: Introduces stratified, layered wall features resembling sedimentary rock bands.

Both.en: Combines erosion breakup with stratified layering for a layered-and-worn look.

Scale.en: The scale of the canyon.

Slot.en: Controls the narrow, slot-canyon component - tightness and emphasis of the deepest cut.
Slot.zh: 窄缝峡谷成分：更深切缝的紧度与强调。

Valley.en: Controls the broader valley form - overall widening and openness of the canyon.

Surrounding.en: Blends the canyon into the surrounding terrain, controlling how much the outer landform influences the final shape.
Surrounding.zh: 峡谷与周围地形的融合程度。

Structual Warp.en: Applies large-scale warping to the canyon structure to introduce bends, meanders, and macro variation.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Formation.en: Applies finer warping to add small-scale distortion and surface complexity without changing the overall canyon layout.

Detail Warp.en: Applies finer warping to add small-scale distortion and surface complexity without changing the overall canyon layout.

Alternate Style.en: Introduces a secondary variation of the selected style to break uniformity and add visual diversity.

Cartography.en: Cartography creates a topographical overlay for a map.
Cartography.zh: 制图风格处理，用于地图化表现。

Map Style.en: Controls the precision of map features such as contours and gradients. Higher values produce more detailed and accurate representations of terrain.

Accuracy.en: Controls the precision of map features such as contours and gradients. Higher values produce more detailed and accurate representations of terrain.

Gradient Style.en: Specifies the style of gradient used to represent elevation or terrain features on the map.

Smooth.en: Applies a continuous, smooth gradient for a natural transition between elevation bands.

LargeContours.en: Emphasizes major elevation bands with broad, distinct contour regions.

AllContours.en: Displays all contour lines, including minor and major bands, for maximum detail.

Equalize Gradient.en: Balances the gradient distribution to ensure even representation of elevation changes across the map.

Reverse.en: Inverts the color or gradient mapping, swapping high and low elevation colors for a different visual effect.

Erode.en: Applies an erosion effect to the map, softening features and simulating natural terrain wear.

Land.en: Selects the color palette used for land areas on the map.

Land Palette.en: Selects the color palette used for land areas on the map.

Classic.en: Uses a traditional cartographic color scheme for land.

Minimal.en: Applies a minimalistic color palette for a clean, modern look.

FertileRed.en: Highlights fertile areas with red tones.

FertileGreen.en: Highlights fertile areas with green tones.

RedBlueSpectrum.en: Uses a spectrum from red to blue to represent elevation or land type.

MineralsYellow.en: Emphasizes mineral-rich areas with yellow hues.

FertileCool.en: Applies cool tones to fertile regions for a subdued effect.

FertileMurky.en: Uses murky, earthy tones to represent fertile land.

Land Contours.en: Controls the visibility and density of contour lines on land areas, highlighting elevation changes.

Land Contour Intenstity.en: Adjusts the brightness or opacity of land contour lines, making them more or less prominent.

Land Bias.en: Applies a bias to the land color or contour mapping, shifting emphasis to certain elevation ranges or features.

Water Palette.en: Selects the color palette used for water areas on the map.

Classic.en: Uses a traditional blue color scheme for water.

BlackSea.en: Applies a dark, deep blue palette reminiscent of the Black Sea.

Caribbean.en: Uses bright, turquoise tones inspired by Caribbean waters.

Water Contours.en: Controls the visibility and density of contour lines in water areas, indicating depth or underwater features.

Water Contour Intenstity.en: Adjusts the brightness or opacity of water contour lines, making them more or less prominent.

Water Bias.en: Applies a bias to the water color or contour mapping, shifting emphasis to certain depth ranges or features.

Trim.en: Removes or crops map features outside a specified boundary, focusing the map on a particular region.

Line Art.en: Sets the number of grid divisions overlaid on the map, controlling the density of the grid.

Grid Count.en: Sets the number of grid divisions overlaid on the map, controlling the density of the grid.

Grid Intenstity.en: Adjusts the brightness or opacity of the grid lines, making them more or less visible.

Grid Style.en: Specifies where grid lines are drawn on the map.

None.en: No grid lines are displayed.

OverWater.en: Grid lines are drawn only over water areas.

OverLand.en: Grid lines are drawn only over land areas.

Everywhere.en: Grid lines are drawn over both land and water areas.

Boundary Thickness.en: Sets the thickness of boundary lines, such as map borders or region outlines.

Contour Thickness.en: Specifies the thickness of contour lines, affecting their visual prominence.

Grid Thickness.en: Controls the thickness of grid lines overlaid on the map.

Cellular.en: Cellular creates cell-based patterns and noises that can be quite versatile as they're ever-present in nature.
Cellular.zh: 蜂窝/细胞噪声，适合岩石破裂与斑块状分布。

Size.en: Controls the overall scale of the cellular pattern. Higher values produce smaller cells (finer detail); lower values produce larger cells (coarser detail).

Density.en: Controls how many feature points are generated per area. Higher density creates more, smaller cells; lower density creates fewer, larger cells.

Jitter.en: Randomizes feature-point placement. Low values are more uniform/structured; higher values create more organic, irregular cells.

Metric Morph.en: Blends between the paired distance behaviors implied by the selected Distance Metric (e.g., Euclidian ↔ Manhattan/Chebyshev), changing cell geometry continuously.

Distance Metric.en: Selects the distance-space used to evaluate the cellular field, affecting the fundamental shape of cells and borders.

Euclidian_Manhattan.en: Morph between rounded Euclidian cells and diamond-like Manhattan cells (axis-aligned, sharper corners) using Metric Morph.

Euclidian_Chebyshev.en: Morph between rounded Euclidian cells and square-like Chebyshev cells using Metric Morph.

Minkowski.en: Generalized metric that spans a continuous family of distance shapes (useful for smoothly varying from rounded to more boxy forms).

Coordinate Axes Jitter.en: Adds jitter in coordinate/axis space before evaluation, warping the field and introducing directional wobble and boundary distortion.

CAJ Clustering.en: Controls how Coordinate Axes Jitter groups together. Low values spread distortion evenly; higher values create patchy/clumped distortion regions.

Anisotropy.en: Stretches the pattern directionally, producing elongated/elliptical cells and emphasizing a dominant direction.

Distance Function.en: Defines what value is output from the cellular field (cell IDs, distances to points, borders, or edges).

Hash.en: Outputs a stable random value per cell region (cell ID-style mask), useful for random patching, selection, and variation.

DistanceInv.en: Outputs inverse distance to the nearest feature point (bright centers fading toward borders).

Distance2Inv.en: Outputs inverse distance to the second-nearest feature point, producing a different internal falloff useful for variation and breakup.

DistanceDiff.en: Outputs the difference between nearest distances (classic Voronoi edge emphasis), great for ridges, veins, and cell borders.

DistanceToEdge.en: Outputs distance to the nearest cell border, ideal for crack networks and edge masks when remapped.

Seed.en: Changes the random distribution of feature points without changing other settings.

Cellular3D.en: Generates three-dimensional cellular noise useful for volumetric-looking patterns and complex terrain breakup.

Size.en: Controls the overall scale of the 3D cellular pattern. Higher values produce larger, more widely spaced cells.

Gap.en: Sets the distance or separation between individual cells, affecting the openness and density of the pattern.

Jitter X.en: Applies random offset to cell positions along the X axis, introducing irregularity and breaking uniformity.

Jitter Y.en: Applies random offset to cell positions along the Y axis, adding variation and natural randomness.

Jitter Z.en: Applies random offset to cell positions along the Z axis, further enhancing the organic appearance of the 3D pattern.

Scale X.en: Adjusts the scale of the cellular pattern along the X axis, stretching or compressing cells horizontally.

Scale Y.en: Adjusts the scale of the cellular pattern along the Y axis, stretching or compressing cells vertically.

Scale Z.en: Adjusts the scale of the cellular pattern along the Z axis, stretching or compressing cells in depth.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating unique variations of the 3D cellular pattern. Changing the seed produces different cell arrangements.

Normalize Input.en: If enabled, normalizes the input values to a standard range before applying the cellular pattern, ensuring consistent results regardless of input scale.

Chokepoint.en: Chokepoint node is a special node whose sole purpose is to help avoid re-connecting many nodes, while adding no memory overhead.
Chokepoint.zh: 强调或塑造狭窄通道/咽喉地形。

Clamp.en: Clamp controls the height of the terrain. You can squash the terrain, clip it at certain heights, or make it taller using the Extend operation.
Clamp.zh: Clamp 控制地形高度：可压缩、在特定高度裁切，或用 Extend 拉高。

Mode.en: Specifies the clamping method used to restrict values within a certain range.
Mode.zh: 限制数值所用的钳制方式。

Standard.en: Applies a fixed minimum and maximum clamp to the input values, preserving their original scale.
Standard.zh: 对输入施加固定最小/最大钳制。

Normalized.en: Clamps and remaps the input values to a normalized 0–1 range, ensuring consistent output regardless of the original scale.
Normalized.zh: 钳制并重映射到归一化 0–1 范围。

Value.en: Sets the clamp threshold or range. Values outside this range are limited to the specified minimum or maximum.
Value.zh: 钳制阈值/范围；超出部分被限制在边界。

Drop.en: Lowers the overall shape to lowest value, ie 'dropping' the entire shape to the 'floor'.
Drop.zh: 将整体形状降到最低值，即“放下”整个形体。

Clip.en: Cuts the terrain against a threshold, removing values above or below a specified level.

CLUTer.en: CLUTer creates color gradients which can be mapped to texture masks to make color maps.
CLUTer.zh: 颜色查找表（CLUT）映射，用于风格化上色。

Reverse.en: Reverses the mapping of the gradient.

ColorErosion.en: Applies erosion-style transport and deposition to color data, creating more natural weathered color variation.
ColorErosion.zh: 结合颜色通道的侵蚀/沉积染色效果。

ColorThreshold.en: Creates a greyscale mask from a specified color range.

Start.en: The color to mask from the given input.

Falloff.en: Range of similar colors to be masked as well.

Combine.en: Combine is one of Gaea's most important nodes. You can combine two terrains (or any node output) using various mathematical operations often known as Blend Modes.
Combine.zh: Combine 是最重要的节点之一：用多种数学/混合模式合并两个地形（或任意输出）。

Ratio.en: The ratio applied to the selected method.
Ratio.zh: 应用于所选混合方式的比例。

Blend.en:
Simply overlays the source on top of the base without extra math.
Direct normal blend; top layer replaces base with alpha control.
Blend.zh: 将源简单叠在底之上，无额外运算。

Add.en:
Brightens by adding the source to the base.
Linear addition of source and base channels, clamped at max.

Screen.en:
Lightens by blending as if projected on a screen.
Inverts both, multiplies, then inverts; 1 - (1 - A) × (1 - B).
Screen.zh: 类似投影到屏幕的滤色提亮混合。

Subtract.en:
Darkens by subtracting the source from the base.
Base minus source per channel, clamps at zero.

Difference.en:
Emphasizes contrast by subtracting lower from higher values.
Absolute difference |A - B| for high-contrast edge-like results.

Multiply.en:
Darkens by multiplying source and base colors.
Channel-wise multiplication; A × B, darkens with stacking.

Divide.en:
Lightens by dividing base by source.
Base divided by source; A / B with normalization/scaling.

Divide2.en:
Alternative division with different scaling for smoother results.
Alternate divide with different scaling/offset to reduce clipping.

Max.en:
Keeps the brighter value at each pixel.
Channel-wise maximum; keeps highest of A and B.

Min.en:
Keeps the darker value at each pixel.
Channel-wise minimum; keeps lowest of A and B.

Hypotenuse.en:
Combines channels using geometric distance for soft blending.
sqrt(A² + B²); Euclidean combination for smooth, bright blend.

Overlay.en:
Combines multiply and screen for vivid contrast.
Combines Multiply and Screen based on base brightness.

Power.en:
Raises base to the power of source for nonlinear effects.
Raises base to source power; A ^ B per channel.

Exclusion.en:
Low-contrast version of Difference for softer inversion.
A + B - 2AB; softer Difference with reduced contrast.

Dodge.en:
Brightens highlights by dividing inverted base by inverted source.
A / (1 - B); brightens highlights aggressively.

Burn.en:
Darkens shadows by inverting, dividing, and inverting again.
1 - (1 - A) / B; intensifies shadows via division.

SoftLight.en:
Gently lightens or darkens based on source brightness.
Conditional blend approximating diffused light on surface.

HardLight.en:
Strong contrast blend combining multiply and screen.
Screen or Multiply based on source brightness threshold.

PinLight.en:
Replaces pixels selectively with lighter or darker values.
Replaces mid-range with source; keeps extremes from base.

GrainMerge.en:
Adds source to base with mid-gray treated as transparent.
A + B - 0.5; mid-gray = no change; good for texture merge.

GrainExtract.en:
Subtracts source from base, centering results on mid-gray.
A - B + 0.5; isolates texture/detail difference.

Reflect.en:
Creates intense highlights by reflecting colors around white.
A² / (1 - B); creates sharp highlight 'reflection' effects.

Glow.en:
Emphasizes bright regions for a glowing effect.
Inverse Dodge-like; emphasizes light bloom by brightening source areas.

Phoenix.en:
Produces a fiery inversion by subtracting and swapping values.
A - B + max(A, B); surreal color inversions with swap-like logic.

Output.en: How to process the data range.

None.en: Retain pure, unclamped data. Less safer, but useful in advanced usage.
None.zh: 保留未钳制的原始数据；进阶有用但更不安全。

Clamp.en: Clamp the data to 0..1 range. Slightly slower, but recommended for safety.
Clamp.zh: 钳制到 0..1；稍慢但一般更推荐。

None.en: No post-processing. Recommended.

Compare.en: Compares two inputs and produces a result based on their relative values.

A/B.en: Ratio of the terrain to compare.

Colorized.en: Show colorized output to signify the modified terrain.

Perpendicular.en: Switch from Horizontal/Stacked to Perpendicular comparison.

Cone.en: Generates a simple conical gradient that is useful as a primitive shape or mask.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size (radius) of the cone.

Height.en: Controls the height (amplitude) of the cone.

X.en: Offsets the cone’s center along the X axis.

Y.en: Offsets the cone’s center along the Y axis.

Constant.en: Constant creates a blank terrain of the height specified, or a flat color output.
Constant.zh: 生成指定高度的空白地形，或平坦颜色输出。

Constant.en: The type of output to create.

Output.en: The type of output to create.

Height.en: Create a flat terrain of the specified height.
Height.zh: 创建指定高度的平坦地形。

Color.en: Create a flat color output of the specified color.
Color.zh: 创建指定颜色的平坦颜色输出。

Height.en: The height of the blank terrain.

Color.en: The color to use for creating a flat, color output.
Color.zh: 平坦颜色输出所用颜色。

Contours.en: Creates map-like contours for a terrain. Useful for making maps or for other overlays.

Count.en: Sets the number of main contour lines to generate. Higher values create more elevation bands across the terrain.

Subdivision.en: Controls the number of subdivisions between main contour lines, adding finer detail and intermediate lines.

Accuracy.en: Adjusts the precision of contour line placement. Higher accuracy produces more exact lines that closely follow the terrain's elevation.

Lines.en: Controls the brightness or opacity of the main contour lines, making them more or less prominent in the output.

Line Intensity.en: Controls the brightness or opacity of the main contour lines, making them more or less prominent in the output.

Sub Intensity.en: Adjusts the brightness or opacity of the subdivision lines, which are the finer lines between main contours.

Line Thickness.en: Specifies the thickness of the contour lines. Higher values produce bolder, wider lines.

Cracks.en: Cracks primitive creates large, cracked patterns on a flat base.
The style of the crack pattern generated by the node.

Style.en: The style of the crack pattern generated by the node.

Normal.en: The default style that creates cracks that gentle slope inward.

Hard.en: The edges of the cracks are not refined and may show aliasing. This may be useful if the softer edges create artifacts in other nodes.

Classic.en: The default style from previous versions of Gaea. This is creates very thin cracks without a slope curve.

Octaves.en: The number of crack pattern sets to generate.

Scale.en: The overall size of the cracked pattern.

Depth.en: The depth of the cracks. It also widens the cracks.

Jitter.en: Control the offset of the cracks between symmetrical and chaotic.

Warp Strength.en: The strength of the warp distortion applied to the cracks.

Warp Size.en: The size of the warp distortion applied to the cracks.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Advanced settings.en: The non-uniform scale on the X axis.

Scale X.en: The non-uniform scale on the X axis.

Scale Y.en: The non-uniform scale on the Y axis.

Craggy.en: Turns a terrain's surface into a craggy, rocky, broken landscape.

Size.en: Controls the overall scale of the craggy features. Higher values produce larger cracked rock formations on the surface.

Depth.en: Sets the depth or prominence of the cracks and rock features, determining how pronounced the craggy shapes appear.

Shape.en: Defines the overall form and pattern of the cracked rock shapes, affecting their outline and distribution.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating unique variations of the craggy rock patterns. Changing the seed produces different results.

Crater.en: Crater primitive creates different types of crater shapes.
Crater.zh: 陨石坑基础体，可生成多种坑体形态。

Style.en: Selects the overall appearance and shaping method for the crater.

New.en: Uses the modern crater generation algorithm, producing more realistic and detailed crater shapes.

Classic.en: Applies the legacy crater style, creating traditional, stylized crater forms.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the crater. Higher values produce larger craters.

Formation.en: Determines the formation characteristics of the crater, such as depth, width, and rim prominence.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation or prominence of the crater above the base terrain.
Height.zh: 相对底面的最大凸起/高度。

Rim.en: Specifies the sharpness and profile of the crater's rim.

Soft.en: Creates a gently sloping, eroded rim for a more weathered appearance.

Sharp.en: Produces a steep, well-defined rim for a freshly formed or less eroded crater.

Shape.en: Defines the overall outline and contour of the crater, such as roundness or irregularity.

X.en: Horizontal placement of the crater or crater field within the terrain.

Y.en: Vertical placement of the crater or crater field within the terrain.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different crater variations.

CraterField.en: Creates a landscape full of craters.

Craterfield.en: Controls the overall size (radius) of craters in the field.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size (radius) of craters in the field.

Depth.en: Controls how deep the craters carve into the terrain.

Density.en: Controls how many craters are generated across the terrain (higher values create more impacts).

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Position.en: Offsets the craterfield along the X axis.

X.en: Offsets the craterfield along the X axis.

Y.en: Offsets the craterfield along the Y axis.

Crumble.en: Crumble runs a different kind of simulation that feeds off of existing crevices, erosive information, and other subtle details to collapse the terrain. Just as the name implies, the terrain starts crumbling from the edges.

Duration.en: Controls how long the simulation runs. Longer durations produce stronger and more extensive crumbling effects.

Strength.en: Defines how intensely the rock or terrain breaks apart from the main body. Higher values result in more aggressive fragmentation.

Coverage.en: Sets how far the crumbling effect spreads inward from exposed edges, determining the affected area.

Horizontal.en: Biases the crumble effect towards flow origins or towards deposits, influencing the lateral direction of collapse.

Vertical.en: Biases the crumble effect towards higher or lower altitudes, controlling whether upper or lower terrain is more affected.

Rock Hardness.en: Controls material resistance, reducing how much terrain collapses. Higher values simulate harder, more resilient rock.

Edge.en: Expands or reduces the impact of crumbling specifically on sharp terrain edges, allowing for more pronounced or subdued edge effects.

Downcutting.en: Controls how deeply the simulation carves downward into the terrain during crumbling, affecting the vertical extent of collapse.

Depth.en: Adjusts the overall depth of the collapsed areas, determining how far the terrain sinks or breaks away.

Direction.en: Specifies the primary direction in which the crumbling effect propagates across the terrain.

X.en: Directs the crumbling effect along the X (horizontal) axis.

N.en: Directs the crumbling effect towards the north (upward in world space).

E.en: Directs the crumbling effect towards the east (right in world space).

S.en: Directs the crumbling effect towards the south (downward in world space).

W.en: Directs the crumbling effect towards the west (left in world space).

Curvature.en: Curvature creates a mask where convex areas (protrusions, sharp edges, etc.) are selected. Very useful layer in texture creation, often as highlights on top of an existing texture map.

Range.en: Sets the minimum and maximum curvature values to include in the mask. Only terrain features within this curvature range are selected.

Type.en: Specifies the type of curvature to evaluate for the mask, determining which terrain features are highlighted.

Horizontal.en: Selects areas with horizontal (planform) curvature, highlighting ridges and valleys based on their plan shape.

Vertical.en: Selects areas with vertical (profile) curvature, emphasizing convex and concave slopes along the direction of steepest descent.

Average.en: Uses the average of horizontal and vertical curvature, providing a balanced mask that highlights both plan and profile features.

Falloff.en: Controls the softness of the mask transition at the range boundaries. Higher values create a smoother, more gradual blend from selected to unselected areas.

Curve.en: Curve adjusts the height curve of a terrain.

Curve Spline.en: Defines the shape of the curve or spline used to remap or adjust values. The curve controls how input values are transformed, allowing for custom response profiles or non-linear adjustments.

Mode.en: Specifies how the curve is applied to the input values.

Absolute.en: Applies the curve using absolute input values, mapping the entire range directly according to the curve shape.

Relative.en: Applies the curve relative to the input's current range or context, allowing for adaptive or proportional remapping.

Fit Curve.en: Automatically fits or scales the curve to match the input range, ensuring the curve covers the full extent of the data.

DataExtractor.en: Extracts specific derived data such as boundaries, differences, or Modifier maps from an input.

Debris.en: Simulates loose debris across the terrain surface to create broken rocky accumulation.

Debris Amount.en: Controls how many individual rocks or debris pieces are emitted across the terrain.

Amount Multiplier.en: Scales the emitted debris amount globally without changing other parameters, allowing quick adjustment of overall density.

Scale.en: Controls the overall scale of debris elements, affecting their size relative to the terrain.

Friction.en: Determines how easily debris slides; higher values make debris stop sooner and form steeper piles.

Restitution.en: Controls energy loss on impact, affecting how far debris bounces or continues sliding after being emitted.

Size.en: Sets the overall size of the emitted rocks or debris pieces.

Height.en: Defines the vertical offset or emission height for debris release.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating varied debris distributions.

Shape.en: Determines the geometric style of debris elements, affecting their appearance.

Render Still Rocks.en: Enables rendering of non-moving debris that has settled on the terrain.

Distribution.en: Specifies how debris is distributed across the emission area.

Uniform.en: Evenly spreads debris across the emission area.

Natural.en: Creates more organic, irregular clustering of debris.

Export Point Cloud.en: Enables the export of debris positions as a point cloud for further processing or use in external applications.

Deflate.en: Compresses and pulls terrain features inward, reducing bulk and prominence.

Amount.en: Controls the degree to which the terrain is compressed or lowered. Higher values result in a more pronounced flattening or reduction of elevation, effectively 'deflating' the terrain features.

Denoise.en: Denoise is a general purpose noise removal filter that systematically cleans up random noise, spikes, and extremely sharp edges.

Type.en: Selects the denoising method used to smooth noise while preserving overall features.

OnePass.en: Runs a single denoise pass for fast, moderate smoothing.

TwoPass.en: Runs a stronger two-stage denoise for cleaner results with better feature retention.

Pixels.en: Targets pixel-level speckle and stair-stepping artifacts, focusing on discrete noisy pixels.

Amount.en: Strength of the denoising effect (higher values smooth more, but can soften detail).

Passes.en: Number of denoise iterations to apply for the selected method.

Dilate.en: Dilate the pixels of the heightfield or mask.

Size.en: Sets the size of the dilation effect. Larger values expand features more, increasing the reach of the dilation.

Shape.en: Specifies the geometric shape used for the dilation operation, affecting how features are expanded.

Iterations.en: Controls how many times the dilation process is repeated. More iterations result in greater expansion of features.

Kernel.en: Selects the kernel type used for dilation, determining the pattern and direction of expansion.

Cross.en: Uses a cross-shaped kernel, expanding features in horizontal and vertical directions.

Rectangle.en: Uses a rectangular kernel, expanding features uniformly in all directions.

Line.en: Uses a line-shaped kernel, expanding features along a specified direction.

LineVertical.en: Uses a vertical line kernel, expanding features only in the vertical direction.

Invert.en: Inverts the input before applying dilation, causing the operation to expand background areas instead of foreground features.

DirectionalWarp.en: DWarp or Directional Warp uses a secondary input to warp the first input in a uniform direction.

Distance.en: Generates a distance field from the input, measuring how far each point is from the nearest boundary or feature.

Method.en: Specifies the algorithm used to calculate distance. Different methods may offer varying performance or accuracy.

Classic.en: Uses the standard distance calculation method, suitable for most general purposes.

RT.en: Uses a real-time optimized distance calculation, providing faster results for interactive workflows.

Mode.en: Determines the pattern or structure of the distance calculation, affecting how distance propagates from the source.

Asterisk.en: Calculates distance in a star-shaped (asterisk) pattern, radiating out in multiple directions.

Pyramid.en: Calculates distance in a pyramid or diamond pattern, emphasizing diagonal and orthogonal propagation.

Directions.en: Sets the number of directions in which distance is calculated, influencing the angular resolution and smoothness of the result.

Skew.en: Applies a skew or bias to the distance field, distorting the propagation direction for creative or technical effects.

Angle.en: Specifies the primary angle or orientation for directional distance calculations, allowing for anisotropic effects.

Angular Jitter.en: Introduces randomness to the angle of distance propagation, creating more organic and less uniform distance fields.

Falloff.en: Controls how quickly the distance value decreases with increasing distance from the source, shaping the gradient of the field.

Threshold.en: Sets a cutoff value for the distance field. Values beyond this threshold are clamped or ignored.

Falloff Jitter.en: Adds randomness to the falloff rate, producing irregular or natural-looking distance gradients.

Options.en: Inverts the input mask or field before calculating distance, reversing the source and background.

Invert Input.en: Inverts the input mask or field before calculating distance, reversing the source and background.

Invert Output.en: Inverts the resulting distance field, swapping near and far values.

Multiply by Input.en: Multiplies the final distance field by the original input, masking or modulating the result.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for any stochastic elements in the distance calculation, ensuring reproducible or varied results.

Distress.en: Adds superficial wear, breakup, and irregular damage to a surface.

DotNoise.en: Generates dotted or speckled noise patterns for texturing and breakup.

Style.en: Specifies the shape of the random elements placed on the surface.

Dot.en: Generates round blobs or spheres, creating soft, circular noise patterns.

Square.en: Generates square-shaped blobs, resulting in blocky, grid-like noise patterns.

Iterations.en: Sets the number of times dots or blobs are placed on the surface. Higher values increase the density and coverage of the noise.

Multiplier.en: Scales the intensity or strength of the dot noise effect, amplifying the contribution of each blob.

Size.en: Controls the average size of each dot, blob, or sphere. Larger values produce bigger features.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation or intensity of the dots or blobs above the base surface.

Blend Mode.en: Determines how the dot noise is combined with the underlying surface or input.

None.en: No blending is applied; the dot noise is used as-is.

Blend.en: Blends the dot noise with the input using standard alpha or linear blending.

Add.en: Adds the dot noise values to the input, increasing elevation or intensity where dots are present.

Subtract.en: Subtracts the dot noise from the input, creating depressions or pits where dots are placed.

Difference.en: Applies a difference operation, emphasizing areas where the dot noise and input differ.

Multiply.en: Multiplies the dot noise with the input, modulating the surface based on dot presence.

Screen.en: Uses a screen blend, lightening the surface where dots are present.

Max.en: Takes the maximum value between the dot noise and the input at each point.

Min.en: Takes the minimum value between the dot noise and the input at each point.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for dot placement and variation. Changing the seed produces different dot patterns.

Draw.en: Draw draws entire mountain ranges in the shape you choose.

DriftNoise.en: DriftNoise is a unique primitive that can create overlapping "shelves". It is a versatile primitive noise that can be used in various scenarios from cliffs to crack production.

Chaos.en: Gives uneveness to the overlapping shelves.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

DuneSea.en: Creates broad fields of dune-like terrain suitable for deserts and wind-shaped landscapes.

Dusting.en: Applies a thin dusting of snow or sediment over the terrain surface.

Snowfall.en: Controls the intensity of the snow dusting effect, determining how visible and thick the light snow layer appears.

Strength.en: Controls the intensity of the snow dusting effect, determining how visible and thick the light snow layer appears.

Snowline.en: Sets the elevation at which snow begins to appear, defining the lower boundary for snow coverage.

Falloff.en: Controls the softness of the transition near the snowline, blending the snow edge smoothly into the terrain.

Distribution.en: Enables or adjusts wind-driven accumulation, causing snow to gather more on one side of terrain features.

Directional.en: Enables or adjusts wind-driven accumulation, causing snow to gather more on one side of terrain features.

Direction.en: Sets the primary direction for wind-driven snow accumulation, simulating the effect of prevailing winds.

Peaks.en: Controls additional snow accumulation on terrain peaks, enhancing coverage on high points.

Coverage.en: Adjusts the overall amount of snow applied to the terrain, increasing or decreasing the extent of dusting.

Slope Coverage.en: Modifies how much snow accumulates on slopes, allowing for more or less coverage on inclined surfaces.

Flow.en: Simulates subtle downhill drift and redistribution of snow, mimicking natural snow movement due to gravity.

Effects.en: Reduces snow coverage in sun-exposed or warmer areas, simulating natural melting patterns.

Melt.en: Reduces snow coverage in sun-exposed or warmer areas, simulating natural melting patterns.

Gritty.en: Adds noise and texture variation to the snow, creating a more natural, patchy, and irregular appearance.

Include Existing Snow.en: Allows the dusting effect to respect and blend with existing snow layers, ensuring seamless integration.

Seed.en: Randomizes the snow pattern, enabling varied results or reproducibility by changing the seed value.

Artistic Control.en: Provides fine-tuning options for the overall look and style of the snow dusting, supporting creative or stylized results.

EasyErosion.en: Provides a simplified erosion workflow for quickly adding natural erosion effects.

Edge.en: Zero Borders softly transitions the edges of a terrain into nothing, similar to a vignette effect in paint applications. Useful when using Bomber or other effects where a tall edge would be problematic.

Style.en: Specifies the shape and profile of the edge effect applied to the terrain or mask.

Round.en: Creates a smooth, rounded edge transition for a softer boundary.

Square.en: Produces a straight, angular edge for a more defined and abrupt boundary.

Precise.en: Applies an exact edge in pixels, preserving sharpness and detail at the boundary.

Size.en: Controls the width or thickness of the edge effect. Higher values create a broader edge region.

Pixels.en: Sets the edge width in pixel units, allowing for precise control over the edge's extent.

Softness.en: Adjusts the smoothness of the edge transition. Higher values result in a more gradual, blended edge.

Equalize.en: Redistributes the input values to balance the histogram and reveal more detail across the range.

Erosion.en: Erosion is the cornerstone of all terrains. It simulates hydraulic erosion and turns any shape into a realistic-looking terrain.
Determines the duration of the erosion simulation. Higher values increase the overall erosion effect, while lower values add subtle erosion details and preserve more of the original landscape.

Duration.en: Determines the duration of the erosion simulation. Higher values increase the overall erosion effect, while lower values add subtle erosion details and preserve more of the original landscape.

Rock Softness.en: Controls the softness of the rock material. Softer rocks erode more quickly, resulting in faster and more pronounced erosion.

Strength.en: Sets the strength of fluvial erosion, controlling the sediment transport capacity. Higher values allow water to carry more dissolved minerals, increasing the rate and impact of erosion.

Downcutting.en: Group containing parameters related to the vertical erosion process, where water cuts down into the terrain to form channels and valleys.

Inhibition.en: Adds restraints to the downcutting process by slowing it down when undissolved sediments accumulate. This results in a mix of deep channels and alluvial fans, depending on local conditions.

Base Level.en: Sets the lowest elevation that downcutting can reach before sediment is deposited. This helps fill large valleys and form valley floors, influenced by terrain slope, altitude, and stream velocity.

Scale.en: Determines the lateral size of the largest erosion features, such as the width of major valleys and ridges, measured in meters.

Feature Scale.en: Determines the lateral size of the largest erosion features, such as the width of major valleys and ridges, measured in meters.

Real Scale.en: Automatically determines the scale from the Terrain Definition, ensuring erosion features are sized appropriately for the terrain.

Terrain Scale.en: Sets the simulated scale of the entire terrain width. Available when Rivers is enabled, this parameter helps match erosion to real-world dimensions.

Verticality.en: Sets the simulated height of the entire terrain. Available when Rivers is enabled, this parameter controls the vertical exaggeration of erosion features.

Flow.en: Controls the amount and behavior of debris generated and transported during the erosion process.

Debris.en: Controls the amount and behavior of debris generated and transported during the erosion process.

Volume.en: Alters erosion physics to treat water flows as volumetric, resulting in higher water levels, wider channels, and more extensive sediment deposits. Useful for forming valley floors without downcutting.

Sediment Removal.en: Removes sediment produced during erosion. This can be modulated using the Sediment Removal mask input to control where sediment is retained or cleared.

Selective Processing.en: Specifies the effect applied when an Area input or Bias is defined. Determines which erosion property is selectively processed.

Area Effect.en: Specifies the effect applied when an Area input or Bias is defined. Determines which erosion property is selectively processed.

ErosionStrength.en: Applies selective processing to the erosion strength, allowing targeted control over erosion intensity.

RockSoftness.en: Applies selective processing to rock softness, enabling localized variation in erosion rates.

PrecipitationAmount.en: Applies selective processing to precipitation amount, affecting how much water is available for erosion in specific areas.

None.en: No selective processing is applied; erosion is uniform across the terrain.

Bias Type.en: Specifies the type of automatic bias to apply when an Area input is not provided. Determines how erosion is distributed based on terrain features.

Altitude.en: Applies bias based on elevation, allowing erosion to be stronger or weaker at different heights.

Slope.en: Applies bias based on terrain slope, enabling more erosion on steeper or flatter areas.

Bias.en: Sets the strength of the bias. For Slope, this controls the steepness threshold; for Altitude, it sets the position from the bottom of the terrain.

Reverse.en: Reverses the direction of the bias, inverting which areas receive more or less erosion.

Other Settings.en: Randomization seed for the erosion process. Changing the seed produces different erosion patterns and channel arrangements.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for the erosion process. Changing the seed produces different erosion patterns and channel arrangements.

Aggressive Mode.en: Enables faster erosion processing at the risk of introducing soft artifacts in minor areas. Useful for quick previews or when speed is prioritized over detail.

Deterministic.en: Ensures the erosion simulation produces the same result every time with the same input and seed, improving reproducibility.

Erosion2.en: An advanced hydraulic erosion node that creates more detailed and realistic erosion results.
Erosion2.zh: 高级水力侵蚀节点，可产生更细致、更真实的侵蚀结果。

General.en: Controls how long erosion runs. Longer durations produce more elaborate terrain reshaping, while shorter durations help preserve original forms.
General.zh: 控制侵蚀运行时长。时间越长，地貌变化越丰富。

Duration.en: Controls how long erosion runs. Longer durations produce more elaborate terrain reshaping, while shorter durations help preserve original forms.
Duration.zh: 控制侵蚀运行时长。时间越长，地貌变化越丰富。

Downcutting.en: Governs how deeply water cuts into the terrain, carving valleys and channels.
Downcutting.zh: 控制水流下切深度，塑造河谷与沟槽。

Erosion Scale.en: Sets the overall size of erosion features, from fine gullies to massive ravines.
Erosion Scale.zh: 设置侵蚀特征的整体尺度：从细沟到巨大沟壑。

Seed.en: Randomizes the erosion pattern while keeping other settings the same.
Seed.zh: 在其它设置不变时随机化侵蚀图案。

Sediment Discharge.en: Fine, light sediments that travel far and fill gullies with subtle detail.
Sediment Discharge.zh: 细而轻的沉积物：可输送较远并填充沟谷细节。

Suspended Load.en: Fine, light sediments that travel far and fill gullies with subtle detail.

Discharge Angle.en: Sets the slope at which suspended load settles.

Bed Load.en: Heavier sediments like gravel that fill and shape gullies and slopes.

Coarse Sediments.en: The heaviest materials (boulders, scree) that deposit on steep slopes.

Shape.en: Enables artistic control over how erosion reshapes terrain.

Shape Sharpness.en: Defines how sharp or concave ridges become after erosion.

Shape Detail Scale.en: Sets the scale of simulated details, from broad ravines to fine gullies.

Orographic Influence.en: Toggles orographic influence on or off.

Enable.en: Toggles orographic influence on or off.

Directional Precipitation.en: Simulates rain falling more intensely from one direction to create rain shadows.

Direction.en: Sets the direction from which rainfall comes most strongly.

Rain Shadow.en: Controls how strongly terrain blocks rainfall from certain directions.

Slope.en: Limits rainfall effects to specific elevation ranges.

Altitude.en: Limits rainfall effects to specific slope ranges.

Reverse.en: Inverts the influence mask for creative control.

Export.en: Exports terrain, masks, or textures to external files.

Format.en: Specifies the file format for the exported output. Choose the format that best fits your workflow or target application.

GaeaRaw.en: Exports the data in Gaea's native RAW format, preserving full precision and compatibility with Gaea.

HalfRaw.en: Exports the data as 16-bit half-precision RAW, balancing file size and detail.

HalfRaw16.en: Exports the data as 16-bit half-precision RAW with explicit 16-bit formatting.

UshortRaw.en: Exports the data as unsigned short (16-bit) RAW, suitable for many terrain and 3D applications.

UshortRaw16.en: Exports the data as unsigned short (16-bit) RAW with explicit 16-bit formatting.

FloatRaw.en: Exports the data as 32-bit floating point RAW, providing maximum precision for advanced workflows.

FloatRaw32.en: Exports the data as 32-bit floating point RAW with explicit 32-bit formatting.

JPEG.en: Exports the data as a JPEG image, using lossy compression for reduced file size and broad compatibility.

PNG8.en: Exports the data as an 8-bit PNG image, suitable for masks and lightweight outputs.

PNG16.en: Exports the data as a 16-bit PNG image, preserving more detail for heightfields and masks.

PNG64.en: Exports the data as a 64-bit PNG image, supporting high dynamic range and advanced workflows.

TIFF8.en: Exports the data as an 8-bit TIFF image, commonly used for masks and simple outputs.

TIFF16.en: Exports the data as a 16-bit TIFF image, suitable for high-quality heightfields and masks.

TIFF32.en: Exports the data as a 32-bit TIFF image, supporting high dynamic range and scientific workflows.

EXR.en: Exports the data as an OpenEXR image, ideal for high dynamic range and professional VFX pipelines.

Location.en: Specifies where the exported file will be saved.

BuildFolder.en: Exports the file to the project's build/output folder.

Custom.en: Allows you to specify a custom folder for the exported file.

Explicit.en: Exports the file to an explicitly defined path, overriding other location settings.

Output Path.en: Defines the full file path or directory where the exported file will be saved.

If File Exists.en: Determines what happens if a file with the same name already exists at the export location.

Overwrite.en: Replaces the existing file with the new export.

Increment.en: Automatically increments the filename to avoid overwriting existing files.

Information.en: Displays additional information or metadata about the export process or output file.

Prepare for Bridge.en: Prepares the exported file for use with the Bridge system, enabling compatibility with external tools or workflows.

Information Houdini.en: Displays or stores metadata related to Houdini integration, such as file attributes or export status.

Extend.en: Expands the terrain range beyond its current limits, effectively stretching elevation values.

File.en: File loads any supported image or data file as a terrain, and supports all major file formats. You can also transform the input.
Specifies the file to load as input for the node. This can be a heightmap, mask, or other supported data file.

Relative Path.en: Defines the file path relative to the project or asset directory, ensuring portability and correct asset referencing.

Is RGB.en: Indicates whether the loaded file should be interpreted as an RGB image. Enable this for color maps or multi-channel data.

Enforce Linear Gamma.en: Forces the loaded terrain or image data to use linear gamma correction, ensuring accurate color and height interpretation.

Allow Unclamped.en: Allows values outside the standard 0–1 range to be loaded, preserving high dynamic range or special data in the file.

Crop to Square.en: Automatically crops the loaded file to a square aspect ratio, which is often required for terrain processing.

Prepare for Bridge.en: Prepares the loaded file for use with the Bridge system, enabling compatibility with external tools or workflows.

Information Houdini.en: Displays or stores metadata related to Houdini integration, such as file attributes or import status.

Caching.en: Clears the cached version of the loaded file, forcing a reload from disk on the next access.

Purge Cache.en: Clears the cached version of the loaded file, forcing a reload from disk on the next access.

Never Cache.en: Prevents the loaded file from being cached, ensuring it is always read directly from disk.

Filter.en: Applies profile-based filtering to reshape terrain values and refine feature response.

Mode.en: Selects the filter response curve used to shape terrain detail by frequency (scale).

LowPass.en: Keeps large-scale forms and smooths out high-frequency detail.

HighPass.en: Keeps fine detail and removes broad, low-frequency forms.

LowShelf.en: Boosts or cuts low frequencies while leaving higher frequencies mostly unchanged.

HighShelf.en: Boosts or cuts high frequencies while leaving lower frequencies mostly unchanged.

BandPass.en: Keeps a band of mid frequencies and attenuates both low and high frequencies outside the band.

Notch.en: Removes a narrow band of frequencies while leaving the rest mostly unchanged.

Bell.en: Boosts or cuts a centered frequency band with a controllable bandwidth.

Frequency.en: The center/cutoff frequency of the filter (controls which detail scale is affected).

Gain.en: Amount of boost or cut applied (used by shelf and bell modes).

Q.en: Filter sharpness/bandwidth (higher Q = narrower, more selective band; lower Q = broader influence).

Keep DC.en: Preserves the overall baseline/average height (DC offset) so the filter affects detail without shifting the mean elevation.

Flip.en: Flip flips the terrain horizontally, vertically, or both.

Type.en: Selects which axis the input is mirrored across.

X.en: Flips the input horizontally (mirrors along the X axis).

Y.en: Flips the input vertically (mirrors along the Y axis).

XY.en: Flips both axes (180° mirror of the input).

FlowMap.en: Generates a modern flow map showing how water or material would travel across the terrain.

Flow Length.en: Controls how far flow paths are traced across the surface (longer values produce longer streams/flow lines).

Flow Volume.en: Controls the amount/strength of flow accumulation used to form the flow map (higher values emphasize major channels).

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

FlowMapClassic.en: Generates a classic-style flow map based on legacy flow behavior.

Fold.en: Fold simulates terrain folding by introducing slants, breaks, and folds to the terrain. It significantly changes the terrain shape and should be used early in the graph.

Waveform.en: Specifies the type of waveform used to apply the fold or wave transformation to the terrain. The waveform determines the shape and style of the folds.

Sine.en: Applies a smooth, sinusoidal wave pattern, creating gentle, rolling folds.

Triangle.en: Applies a triangular wave pattern, resulting in sharp, angular folds with linear transitions.

Sawtooth.en: Applies a sawtooth wave pattern, producing repeating, ramp-like folds with abrupt drops.

Folds.en: Controls the number of folds or wave repetitions applied across the terrain. Higher values create more frequent, closely spaced folds.

Symmetric.en: Determines whether the folds are mirrored symmetrically across the center, producing balanced, repeating patterns.

FractalTerraces.en: FractalTerraces creates fractal terracing on the terrain. It is a powerful alternative to the Terrace node.

Spacing.en: Sets the space between two terraces. Controls the horizontal distance or interval between each terrace step.

Octaves.en: Specifies the number of terraces to generate, including subtle sub-terraces. Higher values create more layers and finer detail.

Intensity.en: Controls the strength of the terracing process. Higher intensities flatten the terraces, making the steps more pronounced.

Shape.en: Defines the general shape of the terraces. Lower values create steeper terraces that follow the terrain's bulk, while higher values produce smoother terraces that protrude outward.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different terrace arrangements.

Advanced.en: Controls how distinctly individual terrace shapes are separated from each other, affecting the clarity of terrace boundaries.

Shapes separation.en: Controls how distinctly individual terrace shapes are separated from each other, affecting the clarity of terrace boundaries.

Macro octaves.en: Sets the number of large-scale terrace layers, influencing the overall structure and major steps in the terrain.

Micro shape.en: Adjusts the fine detail and small-scale shaping of terraces, adding subtle variations to each step.

Character.en: Modifies the overall character or style of the terraces, such as their ruggedness or smoothness.

Thickness uniformity.en: Controls how consistent the thickness of each terrace step is across the terrain. Higher values produce more uniform terraces.

Hardness uniformity.en: Adjusts the consistency of terrace edge hardness, affecting whether terrace boundaries are sharp or soft throughout.

Strata details.en: Adds additional detail to the strata or layers within the terraces, enhancing geological realism.

Protect Range.en: Defines a range within which the original terrain is protected from terracing, preserving natural features in specified areas.

Tilt.en: Enables or disables the tilt effect, allowing terraces to be slanted in a specified direction.

Apply Tilt.en: Enables or disables the tilt effect, allowing terraces to be slanted in a specified direction.

Tilt Amount.en: Sets the degree of tilt applied to the terraces, controlling how steeply they are angled.

Direction.en: Specifies the direction in which the tilt is applied, determining the orientation of the slant.

Tilt Seed.en: Randomization seed for the tilt effect, producing varied tilt patterns when changed.

Warp Amount.en: Controls the strength of the warp effect applied to the terraces, introducing distortion and organic variation.

Warp Size.en: Sets the scale of the warp effect, determining how broad or fine the distortion is.

Warp Style.en: Specifies the style of warping applied to the terraces, affecting the nature of the distortion.

Gabor.en: Gabor noise is one of the lesser used noises, but provides a wonderful pattern-friendly noise that can be used to simulate various aspects of nature.
Controls the scale of the Gabor noise features. Larger values produce broader, more widely spaced patterns, while smaller values create finer details.

Size.en: Controls the scale of the Gabor noise features. Larger values produce broader, more widely spaced patterns, while smaller values create finer details.

Entropy.en: Adjusts the randomness or complexity of the Gabor noise. Higher entropy values result in more chaotic and less predictable patterns.

Anisotropy.en: Determines the degree of directionality in the noise. Higher values stretch the pattern along a specific axis, creating elongated or striated features.

Azimuth.en: Sets the orientation angle (in degrees) for the anisotropic direction of the Gabor noise, controlling the alignment of elongated features.

Gain.en: Controls the amplitude or intensity of the Gabor noise, affecting the contrast and prominence of the generated features.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different variations of the Gabor noise.

Gamma.en: Gamma applies Gamma adjustment to the heightfield, working exactly like Gamma in an image processing program.

The Gamma range is 0.0 to 2.5, with 1.0 being neutral or the original incoming gamma.
< 1.0 lifts mid-values (brighter), expands lighter detail, broadens features.
> 1.0 darkens mid-values, compresses lighter detail, tightens features.

Automatic.en: Tries to automatically set the correct gamma based on existing value.

Gate.en: Defines a baking boundary for the graph by forcing all ancestor nodes to be baked.

Glacier.en: Glacier creates flowing glaciers on mountain tops.

GraphicEQ.en: Reshapes terrain using multiple adjustable bands, similar to an equalizer for height profiles.

Grid.en: Generates a regular grid pattern useful for cartography, masking, or stylized surfaces.

Subdivision.en: Sets the number of grid divisions along each axis. Higher values create a denser grid with more cells.

Line Intensity.en: Controls the brightness or opacity of the main grid lines, making them more or less prominent in the texture.

Sub Intensity.en: Adjusts the brightness or opacity of the subdivision lines, which are the finer lines between main grid lines.

Line Thickness.en: Specifies the thickness of the grid lines. Higher values produce bolder, wider lines.

GroundTexture.en: GroundTexture adds superficial detail to the terrain to increase realism.

Method.en: Specifies the style of ground texture to generate, affecting the overall appearance and character of the surface.

Harsh.en: Creates a ground texture with strong, pronounced features and high contrast, simulating rugged or eroded terrain.

Rocky.en: Generates a texture with rocky details, emphasizing stone-like patterns and roughness typical of stony ground.

Rough.en: Produces a generally uneven and coarse texture, adding subtle irregularities for a natural, weathered look.

Strength.en: Controls the intensity of the ground texture effect. Higher values make the texture more prominent and detailed.

Coverage.en: Adjusts how much of the terrain surface is affected by the ground texture, determining the extent of the effect.

Density.en: Sets the concentration of texture features across the surface. Higher density results in more frequent and closely packed details.

Halftone.en: Converts the terrain or mask into a halftone-style rendered output.

Pattern.en: Specifies the halftone pattern or dithering algorithm used to convert a black and white map into halftone shading. Each pattern produces a distinct visual effect, simulating various print or screen halftone styles.

FloydSteinberg.en: Applies Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion dithering, producing a classic, high-quality halftone effect with smooth gradients.

Riemersma.en: Uses Riemersma dithering, which distributes error along a space-filling curve for a unique, less directional halftone appearance.

O2X2.en: Uses a 2x2 ordered dithering matrix to create a small, repeating halftone pattern.

O3X3.en: Uses a 3x3 ordered dithering matrix for a slightly larger, repeating halftone pattern.

O4X4.en: Uses a 4x4 ordered dithering matrix, producing a more detailed and less repetitive halftone effect.

O8X8.en: Applies an 8x8 ordered dithering matrix for fine, detailed halftone shading with minimal visible repetition.

H6X6A.en: Uses a 6x6 halftone matrix (variant A) for a larger, more complex dot pattern.

H8X8A.en: Applies an 8x8 halftone matrix (variant A), generating a dense and detailed halftone texture.

H6X6O.en: Applies a 6x6 halftone matrix (variant O), producing a unique halftone pattern with distinct dot placement.

H8X8O.en: Uses an 8x8 halftone matrix (variant O), providing a dense and alternative halftone style.

C5X5B.en: Uses a 5x5 circular halftone matrix with black dots, simulating traditional print halftone screens.

C5X5W.en: Uses a 5x5 circular halftone matrix with white dots, inverting the typical halftone dot style.

C6X6B.en: Applies a 6x6 circular halftone matrix with black dots for a slightly larger dot pattern.

C6X6W.en: Uses a 6x6 circular halftone matrix with white dots, providing an inverted halftone effect.

C7X7B.en: Applies a 7x7 circular halftone matrix with black dots, creating a larger, more pronounced dot pattern.

C7X7W.en: Uses a 7x7 circular halftone matrix with white dots, offering a bold, inverted halftone style.

Heal.en: Heal reconstructs damaged, low res, or 8-bit data with 16-bit, high resolution fidelity. It cleans up quantized images with extreme banding of any shape, and yields naturalistic terrain output.

Reconstruction.en: Controls how aggressively missing or damaged areas are rebuilt from surrounding data (higher values preserve continuity but can soften detail).

Passes.en: Number of healing iterations to run; more passes produce a cleaner, more continuous surface but may blur fine detail.

Height.en: Height creates a selection mask within the height range specified.
Height.zh: 按指定高度范围生成选择遮罩。

Range.en: Sets the minimum and maximum elevation values to include in the mask. Only terrain within this height range is selected.
Range.zh: 纳入遮罩的最小/最大海拔。

Falloff.en: Controls the softness of the mask transition at the range boundaries. Higher values create a smoother, more gradual blend from selected to unselected areas.
Falloff.zh: 范围边界过渡柔和度。越高越平滑。

Hemisphere.en: Generates a hemispherical gradient useful for domes, mounds, and radial falloffs.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the hemisphere. Larger values increase the radius and footprint of the shape on the terrain.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation of the hemisphere, determining how tall the dome rises above the base level.

X.en: Adjusts the horizontal position of the hemisphere along the X axis, allowing you to move it left or right within the terrain.

Y.en: Adjusts the horizontal position of the hemisphere along the Y axis, allowing you to move it forward or backward within the terrain.

Flatten.en: Flattens the top of the hemisphere, creating a dome with a plateau or truncated appearance instead of a perfect curve.

Hillify.en: Softens and reshapes terrain into smoother, hill-like forms.

HSL.en: Adjusts the hue, saturation, and lightness of a color input.

Hue.en: Adjusts the hue of the input, shifting colors around the color wheel. Changing this value alters the overall color tone.

Saturation.en: Controls the intensity or vividness of colors. Higher values produce more vibrant colors, while lower values result in muted or grayscale tones.

Lightness.en: Sets the brightness of the colors. Increasing lightness makes the image lighter, while decreasing it darkens the image.

HydroFix.en: HydroFix alters the terrain to create continuous drainage network friendly slopes. It can be used before Erosion or other flow related nodes to get better results.
The amount of downcutting to apply while modifying the terrain for hydrological flow.

Downcutting.en: The amount of downcutting to apply while modifying the terrain for hydrological flow.

IceFloe.en: Icefloe creates flat plates of ice inside a water body.

Size.en: Controls the overall scale of the ice floes. Higher values produce larger ice sheets or floes across the terrain.

Density.en: Adjusts how many ice floes are distributed across the surface. Higher values increase the number of floes per area.

Layers.en: Sets the number of distinct ice layers, allowing for multi-layered ice formations and increased visual complexity.

Thickness.en: Specifies the vertical thickness of the ice floes, determining how prominent or deep the ice appears.

Shaper 1.en: Applies the first shaping function or modifier to the ice floes, affecting their outline and internal structure.

Shaper 2.en: Applies a secondary shaping function or modifier, allowing for additional variation and detail in the ice floes.

Reverse.en: Inverts the effect of the primary shaping function, altering the distribution or orientation of the ice floes.

Reverse 2.en: Inverts the effect of the secondary shaping function, providing further control over the appearance of the ice floes.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different ice floe arrangements.

Island.en: Island draws basic shapes from which entire landmasses can be generated.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Lake.en: Lake simulates rainfall on the terrain and creates physically accurate lakes.

Lake Formation.en: Controls the amount of water available for lake formation, influencing the size and number of lakes generated.

X.en: X position of the lake source.

Y.en: Y position of the lake source.

Render Surface.en: Whether to render the surface of the water or just create masks.

Accuracy.en: The accuracy of the water placement and water containment within depressions.

Precipitation.en: Controls the amount of water available for lake formation, influencing the size and number of lakes generated.

Small Lakes.en: Enables or adjusts the creation of smaller lakes, increasing the frequency of minor water bodies across the terrain.

Flood Control.en: Limits excessive flooding by managing water distribution, preventing lakes from overflowing or merging unnaturally.

Water Floor.en: Sets the elevation of the lake bed, determining the minimum depth and base level of the water body.

Shore Formation.en: Controls the width and extent of the shoreline around lakes, affecting how far the shore transitions into the surrounding terrain.

Shore Size.en: Controls the width and extent of the shoreline around lakes, affecting how far the shore transitions into the surrounding terrain.

Altitude Bias.en: Biases lake placement towards certain altitudes, favoring higher or lower terrain for lake formation.

Size Bias.en: Adjusts the likelihood of generating larger or smaller lakes, influencing the overall distribution of lake sizes.

Layers.en: Combines multiple layers using blend operations in a stacked workflow.

Lichtenberg.en: Creates branching, lightning-like erosion or fracture patterns.

Style.en: Selects the style for the cracks, determining the overall appearance and pattern of the Lichtenberg figures.

A.en: Style A: Produces a classic branching crack pattern, suitable for general terrain fracturing.

B.en: Style B: Generates a denser, more intricate crack network for detailed surface effects.

C.en: Style C: Creates a sparse, wide-spread crack pattern, ideal for subtle terrain disruption.

Scale.en: Controls the scale of the larger cracks, affecting how prominent and wide the main crack structures appear.

Complexity.en: Adjusts the level of detail in the crack network. Higher values produce more branches and finer crack structures.

Depth.en: Sets the depth of the cracks, determining how deeply the cracks cut into the terrain surface.

Expand.en: Expands the cracks outward, increasing their coverage and making the crack network more pronounced.

Bias.en: Provides artistic control over the shape and direction of the cracks, allowing for customized crack patterns.

Seed.en: Random seed for generating the crack pattern. Changing the seed produces different crack arrangements while keeping other settings the same.

LightX.en: Creates a fully lit render using controllable sun, shadow, and ambient lighting.

Direction Selection.en: Specifies how the sun direction is determined for lighting calculations.

Manual.en: Allows manual input of sun direction parameters such as azimuth and elevation.

Geographic.en: Calculates sun direction based on geographic coordinates, date, and time for physically accurate lighting.

North.en: Sets the orientation of the north direction in the scene, affecting geographic sun calculations.

Latitude.en: Specifies the latitude for geographic sun calculations, influencing sun position and lighting angle.

Day of Year.en: Sets the day of the year for geographic sun calculations, affecting seasonal sun position and lighting.

Solar Hour.en: Specifies the time of day for geographic sun calculations, determining the sun's position in the sky.

Sun Azimuth.en: Sets the horizontal angle of the sun, determining the direction from which sunlight is cast.

Sun Elevation.en: Controls the vertical angle of the sun above the horizon, affecting the length and intensity of shadows.

Angular Diameter.en: Specifies the apparent size of the sun in the sky, influencing the softness of shadows and highlights.

Direct Light.en: Adjusts the intensity of direct sunlight in the scene, affecting brightness and shadow contrast.

Shadows.en: Enables or adjusts the rendering of shadows cast by terrain features, enhancing depth and realism.

Ambient Light.en: Controls the overall ambient light level, simulating indirect illumination from the sky and environment.

Ambient Occlusion.en: Enables or adjusts ambient occlusion, which darkens crevices and areas shielded from ambient light for added realism.

Quality.en: Sets the rendering quality for lighting and shadow calculations.

Low.en: Fastest rendering with basic lighting and shadow detail.

Medium.en: Balanced quality and performance with moderate lighting and shadow detail.

High.en: High-quality rendering with detailed lighting and shadows.

Ultra.en: Maximum quality with the most accurate lighting and shadow effects.

Light.en: Adjusts the exposure level, controlling the overall brightness and dynamic range of the rendered image.

Exposure.en: Adjusts the exposure level, controlling the overall brightness and dynamic range of the rendered image.
