Sun Intensity.en: Sets the strength of the sun's light, affecting the brightness of direct illumination.

Ambient Intensity.en: Controls the strength of ambient light, influencing the brightness of areas not directly lit by the sun.

Air Density.en: Simulates atmospheric density, affecting the scattering of light and the appearance of haze.

Haze.en: Adds atmospheric haze to the scene, softening distant terrain and simulating light diffusion.

Ozone.en: Adjusts the ozone level in the atmosphere, influencing the color and intensity of sunlight.

Colors.en: Enables automatic adjustment of sun and ambient colors based on sun position and atmospheric conditions.

Automatic Colors.en: Enables automatic adjustment of sun and ambient colors based on sun position and atmospheric conditions.

Sun Color.en: Sets the color of direct sunlight, allowing for warm, cool, or custom lighting effects.

Ambient Color.en: Specifies the color of ambient light, affecting the overall tone of shaded areas.

Ground Brightness.en: Controls the brightness of the ground plane, influencing the overall illumination and visual balance of the scene.

LinearGradient.en: Generates a straight linear gradient across the terrain.

LineNoise.en: LineNoise is a geometry generator that creates sets of lines which can be distorted and used with other noises and fractals to produce layered ridges.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Mutate Seeds.en: When enabled, the seeds of all nodes within the loop are mutated.

Seed.en: The seed for mutation if enabled above.

MacroPort.en: Defines an input or output port inside a macro for passing height, mask, or color data.

Direction.en: Specifies whether the macro port is used for input or output connections. Determines the flow of data into or out of the macro node.

Input.en: Designates the port as an input, allowing data to be received by the macro node.

Output.en: Designates the port as an output, allowing data to be sent from the macro node.

Display.en: Defines the type of data visualized or represented by the macro port. This helps users identify the nature of the connection in the node graph.

Heightfield.en: Represents terrain elevation data, typically used for heightmaps.

Mask.en: Represents mask data, used for isolating or selecting specific regions in the terrain.

Color.en: Represents color data, used for visual effects or texture information.

Fallback.en: When the given input fails or is intended to short-circuit, return the selected map.

Null.en: Return a null value. May cause node to be disrupted, but needed for Switch and other mechanisms.

Mask.en: Mask draws a mask. If the Input port is connected to another node, a 2D representation of that terrain is shown in the background as a guide. This is optional, as the Input port only provides a drawing guide and does not affect the actual mask.

Match.en: Matches the height range or histogram of one terrain to another.

Mode.en: Specifies the method used to match the height of the current terrain to a reference terrain. Determines how the height adjustment is performed.

Height.en: Directly matches the height values of the current terrain to the reference terrain, aligning elevation point-for-point.

Histogram.en: Matches the height distribution (histogram) of the current terrain to that of the reference terrain, preserving relative features while adjusting overall elevation statistics.

MathX.en: Evaluates mathematical expressions to generate or modify terrain data procedurally.

Expression.en: Math expression or program to execute.

Median.en: Applies a median filter to remove spikes, speckles, and small noise while preserving edges better than blur.

Mesher.en: Mesher can save specific nodes as meshes instead of heightfields, and can also generate LODs.

Format.en: Specifies the file format for the exported mesh. Choose the format that best fits your workflow or target application.

OBJ.en: Exports the mesh in the standard OBJ format, widely supported for 3D models and compatible with most 3D software.

FBX.en: Exports the mesh in the FBX format, suitable for advanced workflows and supporting animation, hierarchy, and metadata.

DAE.en: Exports the mesh in the Collada (DAE) format, an open standard for exchanging 3D assets between applications.

GLTF.en: Exports the mesh in the glTF format, optimized for real-time rendering and web-based 3D applications.

GLB.en: Exports the mesh in the binary GLB format, a compact version of glTF for efficient storage and transmission.

Scale.en: Sets the unit or normalization method for the exported mesh coordinates, determining how the model's size is interpreted.

Normalized.en: Exports the mesh with coordinates normalized to a 0–1 range, useful for workflows that require unitless or relative positions.

Meter.en: Exports the mesh with coordinates in meters, matching real-world scale for compatibility with engineering and GIS applications.

Kilometer.en: Exports the mesh with coordinates in kilometers, suitable for large-scale terrain or geospatial datasets.

Topology.en: Specifies the type of mesh topology used for the exported model, affecting how the surface is constructed and rendered.

Tris.en: Generates the mesh using triangles for all faces, ensuring compatibility with all 3D engines and applications.

Quads.en: Generates the mesh using quadrilaterals where possible, preferred for modeling and sculpting workflows.

AdaptiveTris.en: Uses adaptive triangulation to optimize mesh density, reducing polygon count in flat areas and increasing detail where needed.

Vertices Per Side.en: Sets the resolution of the mesh by specifying the number of vertices along each side. Higher values increase detail but also file size.

Artifact Reduction.en: Applies post-processing to reduce visual artifacts in the mesh, such as smoothing or correcting problematic geometry.

None.en: No artifact reduction is applied; the mesh is exported as generated.

Low.en: Applies minimal artifact reduction, preserving most original detail while correcting minor issues.

Med.en: Applies moderate artifact reduction, balancing detail preservation with improved mesh quality.

Create Normals.en: If enabled, generates normal vectors for the mesh, improving shading and rendering quality in 3D applications.

Create UVs.en: If enabled, generates UV coordinates for the mesh, allowing textures to be mapped accurately onto the surface.

UV Origin.en: Specifies the origin point for the UV coordinate system, affecting how textures are mapped onto the mesh.

TopLeft.en: Sets the UV origin to the top-left corner, matching conventions used in some graphics applications.

BottomLeft.en: Sets the UV origin to the bottom-left corner, standard in most 3D engines and texture workflows.

Create Walls.en: Creates vertical walls along the edges of the mesh, useful for generating closed or extruded terrain models.

Center Pivot.en: If enabled, centers the mesh's pivot point at the origin, making it easier to manipulate in 3D applications.

Level of Detail.en: Specifies the level of detail (LOD) for the exported mesh, allowing for simplified versions to be generated for performance optimization.

None.en: Exports the mesh at full resolution with no LOD applied.

LOD1.en: Exports a simplified mesh with reduced detail, suitable for distant rendering or performance-sensitive applications.

LOD2.en: Exports a further simplified mesh with even fewer polygons.

LOD3.en: Exports a mesh with progressively lower detail, useful for very distant or background objects.

LOD4.en: Exports a highly simplified mesh, minimizing polygon count for maximum performance.

LOD5.en: Exports an extremely low-detail mesh, suitable for extreme distance or preview purposes.

LOD6.en: Exports the lowest possible detail mesh, retaining only the broadest features.

Meshify.en: Converts terrain into a faceted, mesh-like surface with controllable vertex density and detail sensitivity.
Sets the number of vertices used to construct the mesh facets. Higher values produce finer, more detailed meshes; lower values create larger, more pronounced facets.

Vertices.en: Sets the number of vertices used to construct the mesh facets. Higher values produce finer, more detailed meshes; lower values create larger, more pronounced facets.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for mesh facet arrangement. Changing the seed produces different polygonal patterns and facet layouts.

Detail Sensitivity.en: Controls how closely the mesh facets follow the underlying terrain detail. Higher sensitivity preserves more terrain features; lower sensitivity results in smoother, more abstract faceting.

Mixer.en: Mixer allows layer-based manipulation of color textures and contains in-built masking.

Mountain.en: Mountain is one of Gaea's most versatile primitives, using a modulated Voronoi pattern and distortions to create realistic mountain shapes, ready for further modification and erosion.
Mountain.zh: Mountain 是 Gaea 最通用的基础形体之一：以调制 Voronoi 与扭曲生成接近真实的山地形态，便于继续修饰与侵蚀。

Scale.en: Controls the overall size and extent of the mountain. Higher values create broader, more expansive mountain shapes.
Scale.zh: 控制山脉整体尺度与范围。数值越大，山体越宽广。

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation of the mountain, determining how tall the peak rises above the terrain.
Height.zh: 设置山脉最大海拔，决定峰顶相对高度。

Style.en: Specifies the geological and visual style of the mountain, affecting its shape, erosion, and surface features.
Style.zh: 指定山脉的地质/视觉风格，影响外形与表面特征。

Basic.en: Generates a simple, unmodified mountain with minimal erosion or geological detail.
Basic.zh: 生成简洁、少侵蚀感的基础山脉。

Eroded.en: Applies erosion effects to the mountain, creating realistic weathering, gullies, and worn surfaces.
Eroded.zh: 施加侵蚀感，轮廓更自然。

Old.en: Simulates an ancient mountain with softened features, rounded slopes, and significant erosion.
Old.zh: 模拟古老山地：棱角软化、形态更圆润。

Alpine.en: Creates sharp, rugged alpine features with steep faces and dramatic relief, typical of young mountain ranges.

Strata.en: Adds visible geological strata or layers to the mountain, emphasizing sedimentary or volcanic banding.

Bulk.en: Controls the mass and volume of the mountain, affecting how thick or substantial the formation appears.
Bulk.zh: 控制山体体量：偏瘦或厚重。

Low.en: Produces slender, less massive mountains with more delicate features.
Low.zh: 较纤细、体量感较弱的山脉。

Medium.en: Creates mountains with a balanced amount of mass, offering a natural appearance.
Medium.zh: 体量适中、通用的折中设置。

High.en: Generates thick, heavy mountains with substantial volume and broad bases.

Reduce Details.en: Reduces the amount of fine surface detail on the mountain, resulting in a smoother, more simplified shape.
Reduce Details.zh: 减少细碎表面细节，使山体更平滑、更抽象。

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating unique variations of the mountain. Changing the seed produces different shapes and arrangements.
Seed.zh: 随机种子，用于生成不同变体；其它参数不变时仅改变形态细节。

X.en: Offsets the mountain horizontally along the X axis, shifting its position within the terrain.

Y.en: Offsets the mountain horizontally along the Y axis, shifting its position within the terrain.

MountainRange.en: Range primitive quickly sets up an entire mountain terrain with shapes highly optimized for eroding large-scale landscapes.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size and extent of the mountain ranges. Higher values create broader, more expansive ranges.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation of the mountain range, determining how tall the peaks and ridges will be.

Style.en: Specifies the geological and visual style of the mountain range, affecting its shape, erosion, and surface features.

Basic.en: Generates a simple, unmodified mountain range with minimal erosion or geological detail.

Eroded.en: Applies erosion effects to the mountain range, creating realistic weathering, gullies, and worn surfaces.

Stratified.en: Adds visible geological strata or layers to the mountains, simulating sedimentary or volcanic banding.

Alpine.en: Creates sharp, rugged alpine features with steep faces and dramatic relief, typical of young mountain ranges.

Bulk.en: Controls the mass and volume of the mountain range, affecting how thick or substantial the mountains appear.

Low.en: Produces slender, less massive mountains with more delicate features.

Medium.en: Creates mountains with a balanced amount of mass, offering a natural appearance.

High.en: Generates thick, heavy mountains with substantial volume and broad bases.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating unique variations of the mountain range. Changing the seed produces different shapes and arrangements.

MountainSide.en: Generates a single mountain slope or mountainside formation.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size and extent of the mountain slope. Larger values create broader, more expansive slopes.

Detail.en: Adjusts the amount of fine surface detail on the mountain. Higher values add more texture and small-scale features to the slope.

Type.en: Determines the primary form of the mountain feature to generate.

Slope.en: Creates a continuous, sloping mountainside, ideal for simulating the flanks of large mountain ranges.

Peak.en: Generates a prominent mountain peak, focusing elevation and detail toward a summit.

Style.en: Specifies the visual and geological style of the mountain slope, affecting erosion, layering, and surface character.

Basic.en: Produces a simple, unmodified slope or peak with minimal erosion or geological features.

Eroded.en: Applies erosion effects to the mountain, creating realistic weathering, gullies, and worn surfaces.

Old.en: Simulates an ancient mountain with softened features, rounded slopes, and significant erosion.

Alpine.en: Creates sharp, rugged alpine features with steep faces and dramatic relief, typical of young mountain ranges.

Strata.en: Adds visible geological strata or layers to the mountain, emphasizing sedimentary or volcanic banding.

Direction.en: Sets the orientation of the slope or peak, determining which direction the mountain face or ridge is aligned.

Seed.en: Defines the randomization seed for the node, ensuring reproducible or varied mountain shapes with each value.

MultiFractal.en: MultiFractal creates a multi-noise that can have a large level of variations. Often useful for texturing.

Fractal.en: Selects the type of fractal noise used to generate the terrain. Each type produces distinct shapes and features.

Noise Type.en: Selects the type of fractal noise used to generate the terrain. Each type produces distinct shapes and features.

FBM.en: Fractal Brownian Motion. Produces varied, natural-looking noise with a balanced mix of peaks and valleys.

Billowy.en: Creates softer, rounded, and bulbous shapes, ideal for rolling hills or smooth terrain.

Ridged.en: Generates sharp, jagged features, resulting in more dramatic and rugged terrain.

Auto Octaves.en: Automatically determines the optimal number of octaves for the fractal, balancing detail and performance.

Octaves.en: Specifies the number of noise layers (octaves) used. Higher values increase detail and complexity, but may impact performance.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the fractal features. Lower values create larger features, while higher values produce finer details.

Relative Feature Scale.en: Adjusts the scale of features relative to the terrain size, allowing for proportional detail regardless of resolution.

Roughness.en: Determines the roughness of the fractal. Lower values result in smoother shapes, while higher values create more rugged, detailed surfaces.

Edge smoothing.en: Smooths the edges of the generated terrain, reducing harsh transitions and creating a more natural appearance.

Seed.en: Sets the random seed for noise generation. Changing the seed produces different terrain patterns while keeping other settings the same.

Variation.en: Selects the method of applying variation to the fractal.

Type.en: Selects the method of applying variation to the fractal.

SecondaryFractal.en: Uses a secondary fractal to modulate the main fractal, adding additional layers of complexity and detail.

SelfModulation.en: Applies self-modulation, where the fractal modulates itself to create more intricate and unique patterns.

Smoothness.en: Adjusts the smoothness of the variation, with higher values producing gentler transitions and lower values creating sharper changes.

Contrast.en: Controls the contrast of the variation, increasing or decreasing the difference between high and low areas.

Damping.en: Reduces the intensity of variation or modulation, helping to prevent overly chaotic or extreme results.

Bias.en: Shifts the overall output of the variation, allowing you to favor higher or lower values in the resulting terrain.

Position.en: Rotates the fractal pattern, changing the orientation of features across the terrain.

Rotation.en: Rotates the fractal pattern, changing the orientation of features across the terrain.

Anisotropy.en: Applies directional scaling to the fractal, stretching or compressing features along a specific axis.

Offset X.en: Shifts the fractal pattern horizontally, moving features left or right across the terrain.

Offset Y.en: Shifts the fractal pattern vertically, moving features up or down across the terrain.

Warp.en: Selects the type of warping applied to the fractal pattern.

Perturb.en: Selects the type of warping applied to the fractal pattern.

None.en: No warping is applied. The fractal pattern remains unaltered.

Simple.en: Applies basic, soft warping to the fractal, gently distorting features for a more natural look.

Complex.en: Applies advanced, turbulent warping, creating highly irregular and dynamic terrain features.

Relative Size.en: Controls the size of the warp effect relative to the overall terrain, allowing for proportional distortion.

Strength.en: Sets the intensity of the warp effect. Higher values produce more pronounced distortion.

Complexity.en: Adjusts the complexity of the warp, increasing the number of layers or detail in the distortion.

Attenuation.en: Reduces the strength of the warp effect over distance, allowing for localized or fading distortion.

Iterations.en: Specifies how many times the warp effect is applied, with higher values increasing the overall distortion.

Relative Anisotropy.en: Controls the directional scaling of the warp effect, stretching or compressing the distortion along a specific axis.

Noise.en: Noise applies controlled single-pixel noise onto the terrain.

Noise Type.en: Selects the algorithm used to generate noise. Each type produces a distinct pattern and character, suitable for different terrain or texture effects.

Random.en: Generates pure random noise, resulting in a highly chaotic and unstructured pattern.

Perlin.en: Produces smooth, gradient-based noise with natural transitions, ideal for organic terrain features.

Gaussian.en: Applies a Gaussian distribution to the noise, creating patterns with a bell-curve intensity and softer transitions.

Fixed.en: Generates a noise pattern based on large, finite shapes.

Micro.en: Creates very fine, high-frequency noise suitable for adding subtle surface detail or micro-variation.

Height.en: Controls the maximum amplitude or elevation of the noise, affecting how pronounced the noise appears in the output.

Density.en: Adjusts the frequency or scale of the noise pattern. Higher density results in more frequent variations across the terrain.

Relative Density.en: When enabled, density is scaled relative to the current resolution or context, maintaining consistent detail at different scales.

Blend Mode.en: Determines how the generated noise is combined with the input or base layer, affecting the final appearance.

Add.en: Adds the noise values to the input, increasing elevation or intensity where noise is present.

Multiply.en: Multiplies the input by the noise values, modulating the base layer and enhancing contrast.

Subtract.en: Subtracts the noise values from the input, reducing elevation or intensity in noisy areas.

Seed.en: Sets the randomization seed for the noise generation. Changing the seed produces a different noise pattern while keeping other settings the same.

Normals.en: Generates a normal map from the terrain for shading and downstream workflows.

Type.en: Specifies the method used to generate the normal map. Determines the level of detail and the intended use for the resulting normals.

Standard.en: Generates a standard normal map based on the main heightfield, suitable for general use in rendering and texturing.

Detail.en: Generates a high-frequency detail normal map, emphasizing fine surface features for use as a detail overlay or in advanced shading.

Width.en: Sets the horizontal resolution of the generated normal map in pixels. Higher values produce more detailed maps but increase memory usage.

Height.en: Sets the vertical resolution of the generated normal map in pixels. Higher values produce more detailed maps but increase memory usage.

Detail Size.en: Controls the scale of fine details captured in the normal map. Smaller values emphasize finer features, while larger values smooth out detail.

Handedness.en: Determines the coordinate system used for the normal map, affecting how normals are interpreted in different rendering engines.

Left.en: Generates the normal map using a left-handed coordinate system, commonly used in some 3D applications and engines.

Right.en: Generates the normal map using a right-handed coordinate system, standard in many 3D applications and engines.

Up Axis.en: Specifies which axis is considered 'up' for the normal map, ensuring compatibility with different engine conventions.

YUp.en: Sets the Y axis as the vertical (up) direction, matching engines and workflows that use Y as up.

ZUp.en: Sets the Z axis as the vertical (up) direction, matching engines and workflows that use Z as up.

Object.en: Loads external object or mesh data for use inside the graph.

Mesh.en: Specifies the 3D mesh file to import. The mesh will be converted and rendered as a heightfield for use in terrain generation.

Relative Path.en: Defines the file path to the mesh relative to the project or asset directory. Ensures portability and correct asset referencing.

Position.en: Automatically positions the object so its lowest point rests on the terrain base, preventing it from floating or being embedded below the surface.

Drop to Floor.en: Automatically positions the object so its lowest point rests on the terrain base, preventing it from floating or being embedded below the surface.

Offset X.en: Shifts the object horizontally along the X axis, allowing precise placement within the terrain.

Offset Y.en: Shifts the object horizontally along the Y axis, allowing precise placement within the terrain.

Offset Z.en: Moves the object vertically along the Z axis, raising or lowering it relative to the terrain surface.

Scale.en: Group containing parameters for scaling the imported object.

Rotation.en: Rotates the object around the X axis, tilting it forward or backward.

Pitch.en: Rotates the object around the X axis, tilting it forward or backward.

Yaw.en: Rotates the object around the Y axis, turning it left or right.

Roll.en: Rotates the object around the Z axis, spinning it clockwise or counterclockwise.

Quality.en: Enables or adjusts antialiasing for the heightfield rendering, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Antialiasing.en: Enables or adjusts antialiasing for the heightfield rendering, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Occlusion.en: Occlusion behaves similarly to Ambient Occlusion, but favors sedimentary processes vs. lighting.

Strength.en: Controls the intensity of the occlusion effect. Higher values produce deeper and more pronounced shadowing in crevices and low areas.

Octaves.en: Sets the number of detail layers used in the occlusion calculation. Increasing octaves adds finer detail and complexity to the occlusion shadows.

Origami.en: Origami creates a diagonal multifold pattern, and can produce a highly stylized terrain.

Amount.en: The amount of re-folding to be applied to the terrain. Low values create large folds; high values create tiny folds.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different noise patterns.

Outcrops.en: The Outcrops LookDev node creates rocky outcrops on any surface. You can control coverage, breakage, and surface details. Several Outcrops nodes can be layered for complex results.
Controls the number of unique outcrop shapes generated before repetition. Higher values create more visual diversity among outcrops.

Variations.en: Controls the number of unique outcrop shapes generated before repetition. Higher values create more visual diversity among outcrops.

Strata.en: Adds visible geological layering or banding to the outcrops, simulating sedimentary or stratified rock formations. High values increase the distance between Strata layers.

Density.en: Adjusts how many outcrops are placed across the terrain. Higher values increase the number of outcrops per area.

Shape.en: Determines the overall form and silhouette of each outcrop, affecting their appearance and how they blend with the terrain.

Chipped.en: Controls the amount of chipping or breakage on the outcrops, simulating natural weathering and erosion effects.

Seed.en: Sets the randomization seed for outcrop generation, ensuring reproducible or varied results with each value.

Variation Range.en: Specifies the base size of each outcrop, affecting their footprint and prominence on the terrain.

Size.en: Specifies the base size of each outcrop, affecting their footprint and prominence on the terrain.

Height.en: Controls the vertical scale of the outcrops, determining how tall or flat they appear.

Rotation.en: Applies random or specified rotation to each outcrop, increasing natural variation and preventing repetitive patterns.

Pattern.en: Generates repeatable geometric or decorative patterns for masking and stylized terrain work.

Size.en: Controls the overall scale of the pattern, affecting the size of the repeated elements across the terrain.

Dot Size.en: Sets the size of individual dots or elements within the pattern. Larger values produce bigger dots or features.

Spacing.en: Determines the distance between pattern elements, such as lines, dots, or grid cells. Higher values increase the gap between elements.

Steps.en: Specifies the number of discrete steps or repetitions in the pattern, influencing the frequency and repetition of elements.

Direction.en: Sets the orientation or angle of the pattern, allowing you to rotate lines, engravings, or grids as needed.

Type.en: Selects the style of pattern to generate. Each type produces a distinct arrangement of elements.

Lines.en: Generates a pattern of parallel lines, useful for striations or directional effects.

Engraving.en: Creates a pattern resembling engraved or incised lines, adding fine detail and texture.

Grid.en: Produces a grid pattern with intersecting horizontal and vertical lines, forming a tiled appearance.

Dots.en: Generates a regular array of dots, ideal for stippling or point-based patterns.

Pixel Size.en: Adjusts the resolution or granularity of the pattern, controlling how fine or coarse the pattern details appear.

Peaks.en: Creates a mask that isolates the peaks and highest protruding parts of the terrain.

Falloff.en: Controls how quickly the mask transitions from the peaks and ridges to lower altitudes. Higher values create a sharper, more focused mask around the highest points.

Precise.en: Enables a more accurate detection of peaks and ridges, resulting in a mask that closely follows the true tips of the terrain.

Perlin.en: Perlin is the most basic and essential noise. In Gaea, we've made a "geo-variant" by modifying the base Perlin shape to fit the needs of terrain design from the beginning.
Perlin.zh: Perlin 是最基础的噪声。Gaea 提供面向地形设计的“地理变体”，从一开始就更适合做地貌。

Noise.en: Specifies the style of Perlin noise to generate, affecting the overall appearance and structure of the noise pattern.
Noise.zh: 指定 Perlin 噪声风格，影响整体外观。

Type.en: Specifies the style of Perlin noise to generate, affecting the overall appearance and structure of the noise pattern.
Type.zh: 指定 Perlin 噪声风格，影响整体外观。

None.en: <desc>

Scale.en: The scale of the noise. Higher values create larger, less detailed shapes. Lower values create noisier, highly detailed shapes.
Scale.zh: 噪声尺度。越大形状越粗、细节越少；越小细节越密。

Octaves.en: The number of noise octaves. Higher values create more complexity by layering additional detail at smaller scales.
Octaves.zh: 噪声倍频数。越高通过叠加更多层细节而更复杂。

Gain.en: Controls the amplitude reduction between octaves, affecting the persistence and contrast of the noise.
Gain.zh: 控制倍频之间的振幅衰减，影响细节持续强度。

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation or intensity of the noise, scaling the output vertically.
Height.zh: 设置噪声最大高度/强度，垂直缩放输出。

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different noise patterns.

Warp.en: Specifies the style of Perlin noise to generate, affecting the overall appearance and structure of the noise pattern.

Frequency.en: Controls the frequency of the warp, determining how often the pattern is distorted across the terrain.

Amplitude.en: Sets the strength of the warp effect, controlling how far the noise is displaced.

Transform.en: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the noise horizontally.

Scale X.en: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the noise horizontally.

Scale Y.en: The non-uniform scale of the Y axis, stretching or compressing the noise vertically.

X.en: Offsets the Perlin noise along the X axis, shifting its position horizontally.

Y.en: Offsets the Perlin noise along the Y axis, shifting its position vertically.

Pixelate.en: Converts the input into a blocky, pixelated version.

Plates.en: Plates primitive is based on a Perlin core with flat plate-like formations created in between larger Perlin-esque shapes.

Scale.en: The scale of the overall field of shapes. Controls the size of the tectonic plates or regions generated by the node.

Range.en: Adjusts the variation in elevation or intensity between different plates, affecting the contrast and diversity of the generated regions.

Falloff.en: Controls the smoothness of the transitions between plates. Higher values create softer, more gradual boundaries; lower values produce sharper edges.

Warp.en: Applies distortion to the plate boundaries, introducing irregularity and natural variation to the shapes.

Angle.en: Sets the orientation or rotation of the plate pattern, allowing you to control the directional flow of the generated regions.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different plate arrangements while keeping other settings the same.

Pockmarks.en: Creates scattered pits, dents, and small impact-like depressions on the surface.
Controls the average diameter of each pockmark. Larger values produce bigger pits, while smaller values create finer surface detail.

Size.en: Controls the average diameter of each pockmark. Larger values produce bigger pits, while smaller values create finer surface detail.

Scale.en: Sets the overall scale of the pockmark pattern, affecting how widely pockmarks are distributed across the terrain.

Depth.en: Specifies how deep each pockmark is carved into the surface. Higher values create more pronounced depressions.

Density.en: Adjusts how many pockmarks are scattered across the terrain. Higher values increase the number of pits per area.

Multiplier.en: Scales the intensity or strength of the pockmark effect, amplifying the impact of each depression.

Invert.en: Inverts the effect, turning pockmarks into raised bumps instead of depressions.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for pockmark placement and variation. Changing the seed produces different pockmark patterns.

PointCloud.en: Exports the terrain as a point cloud in formats such as PLY, XYZ, or CSV.

Format.en: Specifies the file format used for exporting the point cloud. Choose the format that best fits your workflow or target application.

PLY.en: Exports the point cloud in the standard ASCII PLY (Polygon File Format) format, widely supported for 3D data exchange.

PLY_BINARY.en: Exports the point cloud in binary PLY format, offering smaller file sizes and faster read/write performance compared to ASCII.

XYZ.en: Exports the point cloud as a simple XYZ text file, with each line representing a point's X, Y, and Z coordinates.

CSV.en: Exports the point cloud as a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) file, suitable for use in spreadsheets or data analysis tools.

Scale.en: Sets the unit or normalization method for the exported point cloud coordinates. Determines how the point positions are scaled in the output file.

Normalized.en: Exports coordinates normalized to a 0–1 range, useful for workflows that require unitless or relative positions.

Meter.en: Exports coordinates in meters, matching real-world scale for compatibility with GIS and engineering applications.

Kilometer.en: Exports coordinates in kilometers, suitable for large-scale terrain or geospatial datasets.

Center Pivot.en: If enabled, centers the point cloud around the origin by offsetting all points so that the dataset's centroid is at (0,0,0). Useful for easier manipulation in 3D applications.

Ignore Zero Values.en: When enabled, points with zero or null values are excluded from the export. This helps remove empty data such as the normal low floor of the terrain from the output file.

RadialGradient.en: Generates a circular gradient radiating outward from a center point.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the radial gradient. Increasing the scale expands the gradient outward, affecting a larger area of the terrain.

Height.en: Sets the maximum height or intensity at the center of the radial gradient. Higher values create a more pronounced peak in the center.

X.en: Specifies the horizontal position of the gradient's center. Adjust this value to move the gradient left or right across the terrain.

Y.en: Specifies the vertical position of the gradient's center. Adjust this value to move the gradient up or down across the terrain.

Recurve.en: Recurve is a curvature-based expander that inflates and/or deflates the terrain to create stronger slopes and larger, softer formations from a given noise or terrain.

Power.en: The strength of the inflate/deflate operation. Higher values cause drastic shifts in shape formation.

Scale.en: The amount of details to preserve. Higher values cause more prominent shapes to form.

Repeat.en: Repeat takes a shape and repeats it in a tiled pattern. It is often combined with the Seamless node.

Tiles.en: The number of repetitions on either axis. Controls how many times the input is tiled horizontally and vertically across the terrain.

Compensate Height.en: Adjusts the height of each tile to prevent elevation buildup at tile seams, ensuring a smoother and more seamless repeat pattern.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation for the repeated tiles, allowing you to control the overall height of the tiled output.

Reseed.en: Re-randomizes an upstream procedural node by overriding or refreshing its seed behavior.

RGBMerge.en: Combines three heightfields into a single RGB color output by packing them into separate channels.

Enhance R.en: Selects the enhancement method for the Red channel before merging. Adjusts the contrast and distribution of red values to improve the final output.

None.en: No enhancement is applied to the Red channel. The input values are used as-is.

Autolevel.en: Automatically stretches the Red channel's values to use the full available range, increasing contrast.

Equalize.en: Redistributes the Red channel's values to achieve a more uniform histogram, enhancing detail and balance.

Enhance G.en: Selects the enhancement method for the Green channel before merging. Adjusts the contrast and distribution of green values to improve the final output.

None.en: No enhancement is applied to the Green channel. The input values are used as-is.

Autolevel.en: Automatically stretches the Green channel's values to use the full available range, increasing contrast.

Equalize.en: Redistributes the Green channel's values to achieve a more uniform histogram, enhancing detail and balance.

Enhance B.en: Selects the enhancement method for the Blue channel before merging. Adjusts the contrast and distribution of blue values to improve the final output.

None.en: No enhancement is applied to the Blue channel. The input values are used as-is.

Autolevel.en: Automatically stretches the Blue channel's values to use the full available range, increasing contrast.

Equalize.en: Redistributes the Blue channel's values to achieve a more uniform histogram, enhancing detail and balance.

RGBSplit.en: RGBSplit takes a color node and splits the Red/Green/Blue channels into heightfields. The counterpart to RGBMix.

Autolevel Channels.en: Automatically adjusts the levels of each RGB channel independently, ensuring optimal contrast and brightness for each channel after splitting.

Method.en: Specifies the algorithm used to split the RGB image into separate channels or grayscale outputs.

Average.en: Splits the image by averaging the values of the RGB channels, producing a single grayscale output based on the mean intensity.

BT601.en: Uses the BT.601 standard for converting RGB to luminance, applying weighted coefficients for each channel to match broadcast video standards.

BT709.en: Uses the BT.709 standard for RGB to luminance conversion, applying weights optimized for HD video and modern displays.

RedChannel.en: Extracts only the red channel from the RGB image, outputting its values as a grayscale map.

Ridge.en: Ridge creates a rugged ridgeline with multiple fractures and rock shearing.
Ridge.zh: Ridge 生成带多处断裂与剪切感的崎岖山脊线。

Scale.en: Scale of the ridgeline.

Height.en: Sets the height of the ridge.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Advanced.en: The non-uniform scale of the X axis.

Scale X.en: The non-uniform scale of the X axis.

Scale Y.en: The non-uniform scale of the Y axis.

Rivers.en: Rivers creates a realistic network of rivers with controllable headwaters.

Water.en: The amount of water in headwaters. Higher values can create larger rivers.

Width.en: The width of the rivers. High values create wide rivers, with somewhat wide tributaries. Low values create thin rivers with thin tributaries.

Depth.en: The depth of the rivers. This value is independent of Downcutting.

Downcutting.en: Like with the Erosion node, Downcutting decides how deeply the river should cut into rock and soil while moving forward.

Headwaters.en: The number of headwaters from which rivers can start. Not all will become rivers, but rather tributaries that feed the main river.

Render Surface.en: Whether to render the surface of the water or just create masks.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

RockMap.en: RockMap creates a rock-like coverage mask that can be used to texture terrains on its own or combined with other Data Maps.

Coverage.en: The amount of rock-like formations on the terrain.

Density.en: The density of the rock-like formations.

RockNoise.en: RockNoise is a useful tool for generating fields of rocks with size variations and controllable density.

Size.en: The relative size of the rocks generated by the noise.

Octaves.en: Each octave adds smaller/subdivided rocks in between the larger ones from the previous octave.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Rockscape.en: Creates broad rocky surface formations and broken stone-like terrain detail.

Size.en: Controls the overall scale of the rock formations. Higher values produce larger, more expansive rock features.

Erosion.en: Adjusts the amount of erosion applied to the rockscape, simulating natural weathering and smoothing of rock surfaces.

Breakage.en: Determines the degree of fracturing and splitting in the rocks, creating more jagged and broken surfaces as the value increases.

Roughness.en: Sets the surface roughness of the rocks, adding fine detail and texture to the formations.

Jitter.en: Introduces randomness to the placement and shape of rock features, making the rockscape appear more natural and less uniform.

Clusters.en: Controls the clustering behavior of rock formations, affecting how rocks group together or remain isolated.

Off.en: Disables clustering, resulting in evenly distributed rock features.

Large.en: Creates large clusters of rocks, forming prominent groupings and massifs.

Small.en: Generates small, tight clusters of rocks, producing scattered groupings across the surface.

Shattered.en: Simulates shattered rock formations, with highly fragmented and irregular clusters.

Relief.en: Specifies the style of surface relief, affecting the sharpness and layering of the rockscape.

Off.en: No additional relief is applied; the surface remains as generated by the base parameters.

Sharp.en: Applies sharp, pronounced relief, emphasizing angular features and steep transitions.

Soft.en: Applies soft, gentle relief, smoothing out transitions and creating a more weathered appearance.

Stratified.en: Adds visible stratification or layering to the rockscape, simulating sedimentary or banded rock formations.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating unique variations of the rockscape. Changing the seed produces different rock patterns.

Roughen.en: Adds fine roughness and small-scale breakup to the terrain surface.

Route.en: Route chooses the flow of the graph based on the Input/Output ports chosen, and relies on integer input for automation.

Choice.en: The port through which the input should be routed.

Rugged.en: Rugged is a very powerful primitive node that creates a strong, rocky surface for any terrain while preserving overall shape.

Scale.en: The size of the geological features.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Sand.en: Sand creates medium and small level sand patterns. It can also be used to simulate dunes.

Scale.en: The scale of the sand pattern.

Height.en: The height of the sand pattern.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Sandstone.en: Creates layered sandstone-like terracing and sedimentary rock structure.
Sandstone.zh: 生成层状砂岩式阶地与沉积岩结构。

Passes.en: Sets the number of erosion passes applied to simulate layered sandstone formation. More passes increase the detail and realism of the stratified effect.
Passes.zh: 模拟层状砂岩的侵蚀遍数。

Iterations.en: Controls how many times the erosion process is repeated within each pass, refining the sandstone layering and surface features.
Iterations.zh: 每遍内侵蚀过程重复次数。

Spacing.en: Determines the distance between individual sandstone layers, affecting the frequency and thickness of visible strata.
Spacing.zh: 砂岩层间距，影响层理频率。

Intensity.en: Adjusts the overall strength of the sandstone effect, influencing how pronounced the layers and erosion features appear.

Convexity.en: Controls the curvature of the sandstone layers, making them appear more rounded (convex) or flat.

Tilt.en: Applies an angular tilt to the sandstone layers, simulating geological tilting or shifting of strata.
Tilt.zh: 岩层倾斜角，模拟地质掀斜。

Direction.en: Sets the orientation of the sandstone layers, determining the primary direction in which the strata are aligned.

Chaos.en: Introduces randomness and irregularity to the sandstone layers, creating a more natural and less uniform appearance.

Seed.en: Defines the randomization seed for procedural generation, ensuring unique but repeatable sandstone patterns.

Chipped.en: Enables or controls the presence of chipped or broken edges in the sandstone, simulating natural weathering and breakage.

Chipping.en: Adjusts the amount and detail of chipping applied to the sandstone layers, affecting the roughness and realism of eroded edges.

SatMap.en: Generates terrain color from preset satellite-style palettes with controllable range and processing.
SatMap.zh: 用可控范围与处理，从卫星风格预设色板生成地形颜色。

None.en: <desc>
<desc>

Scree.en: Creates accumulations of loose rock fragments scattered across slopes and terrain edges.

Stones.en: Controls the overall size of the scree stones. Higher values produce larger rock fragments, while lower values create finer gravel.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the scree stones. Higher values produce larger rock fragments, while lower values create finer gravel.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation or prominence of the scree stones above the terrain surface.

Density.en: Adjusts how many scree stones are distributed across the surface. Higher values increase the number of stones per area.

Spread.en: Determines how widely the scree stones are scattered from their source, affecting the coverage area and natural dispersion.

Edge.en: Controls the accumulation of scree along terrain edges or boundaries, allowing for more pronounced deposits at the base of slopes or cliffs.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for scree placement and variation. Changing the seed produces different scree patterns.

Sea.en: Sea is a multi-function water surface generator and coastal erosion tool. Its primary purpose is to create a water surface, while Coastal Erosion creates beaches and cliffs.
The main Sea node, responsible for generating the sea area in the terrain. Contains options to control the global and surrounding sea behavior.

Global.en: Enables the sea to cover the entire terrain globally, overriding local variations.

Surrounding.en: Restricts the sea to only surround the terrain, creating a border or coastal effect rather than filling the entire area.

Level.en: Controls the water level of the sea. Higher values raise the sea, submerging more terrain, while lower values expose more land.

Coastal Erosion.en: Applies erosion to the coastal areas where the sea meets the land, simulating natural shoreline wear and shaping.

Shore Size.en: Determines the width of the shore created by coastal erosion. Larger values produce broader beaches or transition zones.

Shore Height.en: Sets the elevation difference between the sea level and the top of the shore, affecting the steepness of the coastline.

Variation.en: Controls the amount of natural variation and irregularity along the coastline, making the shore appear more organic and less uniform.

Uniform Variations.en: When enabled, applies consistent variation along the entire coast, resulting in a more uniform shoreline appearance.

Extra Cliff Details.en: Adds additional detail and features to cliffs along the coast, enhancing realism and visual interest in steep shoreline areas.

Render Surface.en: Determines whether the sea surface is rendered in the final terrain output. Enable to visualize the water surface.

Seamless.en: Seamless can transform any input terrain or color map into a tileable/repeating pattern.

Edge.en: The amount of blending across the opposite edges.

Shift X.en: Shift blending on the X axis.

Shift Y.en: Shift blending on the Y axis.

Sediments.en: Sediments creates a thick layer of generic sedimentation on top of the terrain, which can be used for sand or snow.

Shade.en: Produces a shaded terrain render based on lighting direction and surface relief.

Render Style.en: Specifies the shading technique used to render the terrain. Each style provides a different visual representation for analysis or artistic purposes.

TableTop.en: Renders the terrain for a stylized overview.

HillShade.en: Applies traditional hillshading to simulate sunlight and shadow, enhancing the perception of terrain relief and surface features.

Occlusion.en: Highlights areas of the terrain that are occluded or in shadow, useful for analyzing light accessibility and terrain exposure.

SoftLight.en: Uses a soft, diffuse lighting model to gently illuminate the terrain, reducing harsh shadows and creating a more natural look.

Sun Azimuth.en: Sets the horizontal angle of the sun in degrees, determining the direction from which sunlight is cast across the terrain.

Sun Elevation.en: Controls the vertical angle of the sun above the horizon, affecting the length and intensity of shadows on the terrain.

Sunlight.en: Adjusts the overall intensity or brightness of direct sunlight in the shading calculation.

Shade Bias.en: Offsets the shading calculation to reduce or increase shadow strength, helping to fine-tune the balance between light and dark areas.

Soft Shadows.en: Enables or adjusts the softness of shadows, creating more gradual transitions between light and shadow for a realistic effect.

Reflected Light.en: Simulates indirect illumination by adding light reflected from surrounding terrain, enhancing realism and reducing overly dark shadowed areas.

High Quality.en: Enables high-quality rendering for shading, using more advanced calculations for smoother gradients and more accurate lighting effects.

Shape.en: Generates basic geometric terrain shapes for use as primitives or masks.

Geometry.en: Specifies the base geometric shape used for the node. Determines the fundamental outline or profile of the generated object.

Circle.en: Generates a circular shape as the base geometry, resulting in round or elliptical forms.

Rectangle.en: Generates a rectangular shape as the base geometry, resulting in box-like or elongated forms.

Sides.en: Defines the number of sides for polygonal shapes. Higher values create shapes closer to a circle, while lower values produce more angular forms.

Uniform.en: When enabled, ensures that scaling and transformations are applied equally in all directions, maintaining the original proportions of the shape.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the shape, scaling it uniformly along both the X and Y axes.

Scale X.en: Adjusts the width of the shape by scaling it along the X axis independently.

Scale Y.en: Adjusts the height of the shape by scaling it along the Y axis independently.

Thickness.en: Specifies the thickness of the shape's outline or border, or the width of a ring for hollow shapes.

Height.en: Sets the vertical extent or elevation of the shape, often used to define extrusion or relief in terrain generation.

X.en: Sets the horizontal position or offset of the shape along the X axis.

Y.en: Sets the vertical position or offset of the shape along the Y axis.

Shaper.en: Shaper bulks up or bulks down a terrain, while optionally retaining the finer details.

Shape.en: Negative values will bulk down the shape, while positive values will bulk up the shape.

Local Effect.en: Limits the shaping effect to localized regions instead of applying it globally, allowing for targeted adjustments.

Local Area.en: Specifies the size or extent of the local region affected when 'Local Effect' is enabled. Larger values increase the area of influence.

Maintain Fine Details.en: When enabled, finer detail is preserved regardless of shape changes.

Detail Size.en: Controls the scale of details to be preserved or affected during shaping. Smaller values focus on finer details, while larger values affect broader features.

Sharpen.en: Sharpen enhances terrain edges and small structures by making them more prominent.

Method.en: Selects the sharpening technique to apply to the terrain or texture. Each method targets different aspects of the data for sharpening.

Edge.en: Sharpens the terrain or texture by enhancing edges, making transitions between features more pronounced.

Frequency.en: Sharpens by boosting high-frequency details, increasing the clarity of fine structures and textures.

Amount.en: The amount of sharpening to be applied to the structures. Higher values produce a stronger sharpening effect.

Shatter.en: Shatter transforms simple shapes into complex, highly eroded, and fractured terrains.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Shear.en: Shear creates rock shearing and exposes strata.

Strength.en: The amount of terrain warp/shear that will be applied.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Shrubs.en: Adds low vegetation or shrub-like surface growth across the terrain.
Specifies the number of shrubs to generate, in thousands. Controls the overall density of shrubs across the terrain.

Count in Thousands.en: Specifies the number of shrubs to generate, in thousands. Controls the overall density of shrubs across the terrain.

Is Relative.en: If enabled, the shrub count is relative to the terrain size or other factors, rather than being an absolute number.

Shape.en: Determines the shape or type of shrub clusters to be placed. Affects the visual appearance and distribution pattern of shrubs.

Point.en: Places individual shrubs as single points, resulting in a scattered, sparse distribution.

Big.en: Generates larger shrub clusters, simulating denser or more mature shrub growth.

BigOnly.en: Restricts placement to only large shrub clusters, omitting individual or small shrubs.

Seed.en: Sets the randomization seed for shrub placement, ensuring reproducible or varied results.

Growth.en: Determines how shrubs respond to water sources, influencing their tendency to grow near or away from water.

Seek Water.en: Determines how shrubs respond to water sources, influencing their tendency to grow near or away from water.

Seek.en: Shrubs preferentially grow closer to water sources, increasing density near moist areas.

Avoid.en: Shrubs avoid water sources, resulting in sparser growth near moist areas.

Avoid Trees.en: Controls how shrubs interact with tree placement, affecting their distribution relative to trees.

None.en: Shrubs are placed without regard to tree locations.

Previous.en: Shrubs avoid areas where trees were previously placed, reducing overlap.

All.en: Shrubs avoid all tree-covered areas, ensuring no overlap between shrubs and trees.

Health.en: Represents the overall health or vigor of shrubs, affecting their size, density, and appearance.

Spread.en: Controls how far shrubs can spread from their initial placement, influencing patch size and coverage.

Random.en: Introduces randomness to shrub placement and growth, creating more natural and varied patterns.

Simulation Bias.en: Adjusts the simulation to favor certain environmental conditions or behaviors, influencing shrub distribution.

Aspect Inhibition.en: Limits shrub growth on steep slopes, simulating natural growth patterns where shrubs prefer gentler terrain.

Slope.en: Limits shrub growth on steep slopes, simulating natural growth patterns where shrubs prefer gentler terrain.

Slope Falloff.en: Controls how quickly shrub density decreases as slope increases.

Altitude.en: Restricts shrub growth above or below certain altitudes, simulating elevation-based vegetation zones.

Altitude Falloff.en: Controls the rate at which shrub density decreases with altitude.

Snow Inhibition.en: Prevents shrub growth in areas with stagnant or 'dead' water flow, simulating natural avoidance of such regions.

Dead Flow.en: Prevents shrub growth in areas with stagnant or 'dead' water flow, simulating natural avoidance of such regions.

Consolidate Flows.en: Encourages shrubs to grow along consolidated water flow paths, such as stream banks or drainage lines.

Bias.en: Applies a directional or environmental bias to shrub placement, favoring certain areas or conditions.

Artistic Control.en: Increases the irregularity and unpredictability of shrub placement, creating a more natural look.

Chaos.en: Increases the irregularity and unpredictability of shrub placement, creating a more natural look.

Blur Edges.en: Softens the boundaries of shrub patches, blending them more smoothly into the surrounding terrain.

Custom Inhibitors.en: Allows custom input maps or masks to influence shrub placement and density.

Custom Influence.en: Allows custom input maps or masks to influence shrub placement and density.

Trim.en: Removes or reduces shrubs in specified areas, providing manual control over final distribution.

Slope.en: Slope creates a selection mask within the slope range specified.
Slope.zh: 按指定坡度范围生成选择遮罩。

Range.en: Sets the minimum and maximum slope angles to include. Only terrain within this range is selected in the mask.

Falloff.en: Controls the soft transition at the range boundaries. Higher values create a smoother, more gradual blend from selected to unselected areas.

Type.en: Defines the slope calculation method, affecting how the mask interprets and distributes slope values.
Type.zh: 坡度计算方式，影响遮罩分布。

Accurate.en: Uses precise slope computation for more realistic, detail-preserving results.
Accurate.zh: 更精确的坡度计算，细节更真实。

Normalized.en: Produces a consistent, even distribution across the slope range, useful for stylized or uniform masks.
Normalized.zh: 在坡度范围内更均匀一致的分布。

Micro Accent.en: Enhances fine details and subtle variations in the slope mask, adding extra texture and definition to small-scale features.
Micro Accent.zh: 增强坡度遮罩中的细微变化。

SlopeBlur.en: SlopeBlur is a versatile, low-level node that adds directional blurring based on the slopes of a Guide terrain or mask. It is one of our deceptively simple nodes that can create a wide array of shapes.

Intensity.en: Controls the strength of the slope blur effect. Higher values result in more pronounced blurring along the slope direction.

Iterations.en: Specifies how many times the slope blur operation is applied. More iterations increase the smoothness and diffusion of the blur.

Direction.en: Sets the primary direction in which the blur is applied. Adjusting this value changes the orientation of the blur effect across the terrain.

Asymmetry.en: Controls the asymmetry of the blur, allowing the effect to be stronger in one direction than the other for more natural or stylized results.

Box.en: Uses a box-shaped window for uniform blurring, resulting in sharper transitions at the edges.

Quality.en: Settings related to the quality and precision of the slope blur operation. Higher quality may increase processing time but results in smoother, more accurate blurring.

Antialiasing.en: Applies antialiasing to the slope blur effect, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Off.en: No antialiasing is applied. May result in sharper but potentially jagged edges.

x4.en: Applies 4x antialiasing for moderate smoothing of edges.

x16.en: Applies 16x antialiasing for maximum edge smoothing and highest visual quality.

SlopeWarp.en: SlopeBlur is a versatile, low-level node that adds directional warping based on the slopes of a Guide terrain or mask. It behaves similarly to SlopeBlur.

Intensity.en: Controls the strength of the slope warp effect. Higher values produce more pronounced warping and distortion of the terrain along the slope.

Iterations.en: Specifies how many times the slope warp operation is applied. Increasing iterations can create more complex or exaggerated warping effects.

Direction.en: Sets the primary direction in which the slope warp is applied. Adjust this to control the orientation of the warping across the terrain.

Normalized.en: When enabled, normalizes the effect so that the intensity is consistent regardless of terrain scale or resolution.

Quality.en: Settings related to the quality and precision of the slope warp operation. Higher quality may increase processing time but results in smoother, more accurate warping.

Antialiasing.en: Applies antialiasing to the slope warp effect, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Off.en: No antialiasing is applied. May result in sharper but potentially jagged edges.

x4.en: Applies 4x antialiasing for moderate smoothing of edges.

x16.en: Applies 16x antialiasing for maximum edge smoothing and highest visual quality.

Slump.en: Slump is a simple primitive that creates relative smooth hills with slumped (collapsed) areas. It is very useful for creating large landscapes.

Scale.en: The scale of the slump.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Snow.en: Snow simulates snow fall, melt, and settling like in nature, and controls how the snow adheres and flows along the terrain.
Snow.zh: 模拟降雪、融雪与沉降，并控制积雪如何附着与沿地形流动。

Snow.en: Controls the length of time snow accumulates on the terrain, affecting overall snow coverage and depth.
Snow.zh: 积雪累积时间，影响整体雪量。

Duration.en: Controls the length of time snow accumulates on the terrain, affecting overall snow coverage and depth.
Duration.zh: 积雪累积时间，影响整体雪量。

Intensity.en: Determines the rate at which snow falls and accumulates, influencing the thickness and density of the snow layer.
Intensity.zh: 降雪与堆积速率，影响厚度。

Settle Duration.en: Specifies the time it takes for freshly fallen snow to settle and compact, impacting the smoothness and stability of the snow surface.
Settle Duration.zh: 新雪沉降压实所需时间。

Melt.en: Defines the method by which snow melts from the terrain, affecting the pattern and distribution of melting.
Melt.zh: 融雪方式，影响融雪图案与分布。

Melt Type.en: Defines the method by which snow melts from the terrain, affecting the pattern and distribution of melting.
Melt Type.zh: 融雪方式，影响融雪图案与分布。

Uniform.en: Snow melts evenly across the entire terrain, resulting in a consistent reduction of snow coverage.

Directional.en: Snow melts preferentially in a specific direction, simulating effects such as sun exposure or wind, leading to uneven snow retreat.

Melt Remnants.en: Specifies the amount and appearance of snow left behind after melting, such as patches or traces of residual snow.

Direction.en: Sets the primary direction for directional melting, influencing which areas of the terrain lose snow first.

Snow Line.en: Defines the altitude or threshold below which snow does not accumulate, simulating natural snow lines on mountains.

Advanced.en: Specifies the minimum slope angle at which snow will slide off, affecting snow accumulation on steep surfaces.

Slip-off angle.en: Specifies the minimum slope angle at which snow will slide off, affecting snow accumulation on steep surfaces.

Adhered snow mass.en: Controls the amount of snow that remains attached to surfaces, even on steep or vertical terrain.

Model scale.en: Sets the scale of the terrain model, influencing how snow parameters are interpreted relative to real-world dimensions.

Real Scale.en: Specifies the actual physical scale represented by the terrain, used for accurate snow simulation and parameter scaling.

Terrain Scale.en: Adjusts the scaling factor for the terrain, affecting how snow features are distributed and visualized.

Verticality.en: Controls the influence of vertical surfaces on snow accumulation, determining how much snow can adhere to cliffs and steep slopes.

Seed.en: Sets the randomization seed for snow distribution, ensuring reproducible results or introducing variation in snow patterns.

Snowfield.en: Creates broad settled snow coverage across the terrain surface.

SoftClip.en: SoftClip a low-level utility that lets you softly reduce the intensity of shapes above a specified threshold. It can be comparable to masking a shape with a Height node and then clamping that portion.

Clip Mode.en: Selects whether the soft clipping effect is applied above or below the specified threshold.

AboveThreshold.en: Applies soft clipping to values above the threshold, gently compressing high values toward the threshold.

BelowThreshold.en: Applies soft clipping to values below the threshold, gently compressing low values toward the threshold.

Threshold.en: Sets the value at which soft clipping begins. Values above or below this threshold (depending on mode) will be affected.

Softness.en: Controls the smoothness of the transition at the threshold. Higher values create a more gradual, less abrupt clipping effect.

Clipping.en: Adjusts the overall strength of the clipping effect, determining how much values are compressed toward the threshold.

Soil.en: Soil Map creates a soil mask, with increased density in crevices or other areas where the slope allows soil to settle.

Splat.en: Splat is similar to RGBMix, taking heightfield nodes and encoding them to the RGB channels of a color map, and providing properties to control the inputs.

Autolevel.en: Automatically adjusts the levels of the combined channels to maximize the output range.

Clamp Product.en: Clamps the product of the R, G, and B channels to the 0..1 range, ensuring the output does not exceed valid limits.

Steps.en: Creates stepped formations and hard terrace-like breaks in the terrain.
Controls the overall size and spacing of the steps. Higher values produce larger, more widely spaced terraces, while lower values create finer, closely packed steps.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size and spacing of the steps. Higher values produce larger, more widely spaced terraces, while lower values create finer, closely packed steps.

Density.en: Determines the number of steps or terraces within the terrain. Increasing density results in more steps, creating a more detailed and intricate terraced effect.

Seed.en: Sets the random seed for the step pattern. Changing the seed generates a different arrangement of steps while keeping other settings the same.

Stones.en: Scatters stones or small rock forms across the surface.
Controls the overall size of the stones. Higher values produce larger stones, while lower values create finer gravel.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the stones. Higher values produce larger stones, while lower values create finer gravel.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation or prominence of the stones above the terrain surface.

Density.en: Adjusts how many stones are scattered across the surface. Higher values increase the number of stones per area.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for stone placement and variation. Changing the seed produces different stone patterns.

Stratify.en: Stratify creates broken strata or rock layers on the terrain in a non-linear fashion, producing a robust, realistic formation.

Spacing.en: Controls the distance between individual stratified layers, affecting the frequency and thickness of visible strata in the terrain.

Octaves.en: Sets the number of noise octaves used to add variation to the stratified layers. Higher values introduce more complexity and detail.

Intensity.en: Adjusts the overall strength of the stratification effect, making the layers more or less pronounced.

Shape.en: Modifies the profile or contour of the stratified layers, influencing how sharply or smoothly the layers transition.

Seed.en: Defines the randomization seed for procedural generation, ensuring unique but repeatable stratification patterns.

Tilt Amount.en: Applies an angular tilt to the stratified layers, simulating geological tilting or shifting of strata.

Direction.en: Sets the orientation of the stratified layers, determining the primary direction in which the strata are aligned.

Sunlight.en: Sunlight is a Data Map that gives you the sunlight integral (sun light/shadow map) of any given period (up to 365 days). It can be used to drive snow melt, vegetation growth, and more.

North.en: Specifies the direction considered as 'north' for sunlight calculations. Adjusting this affects the orientation of shadows and lighting in the terrain.

Year.en: Sets the year for solar position calculations. This can influence the sun's path and seasonal lighting effects on the terrain.

Latitude.en: Defines the latitude of the terrain location. Changing the latitude alters the angle and intensity of sunlight, simulating different geographic regions.

SuperColor.en: Applies procedural terrain colorization using texture, flow, peaks, and palette controls.

None.en: <desc>

Swirl.en: Swirl creates a vortex warp on the terrain. Very useful for adding a fluid look.

Switch.en: Switch chooses between two different heightfield inputs and relies on a boolean (true/false) input.

Switch Route.en: Selects which input route is active. Use this to dynamically switch between different input sources or branches in your graph.

Discard Alt in Final Build.en: If enabled, alternate (inactive) input routes are discarded during the final build, reducing memory usage and export size.

Synth.en: Synth takes a bitmap image (photo or artwork) and converts it to CLUT map that can be used with a texture mask to colorize your terrain.

Data.en: Input data for the node, such as source terrain or mask information.

Sampling.en: Specifies the number of color stops or samples in the synthesized gradient. Higher values produce smoother gradients.

Samples.en: Specifies the number of color stops or samples in the synthesized gradient. Higher values produce smoother gradients.

_8.en: Generates a gradient with 8 color stops. Suitable for coarse transitions.

_16.en: Generates a gradient with 16 color stops. Provides a moderately smooth transition.

_24.en: Generates a gradient with 24 color stops. Offers finer color transitions.

_36.en: Generates a gradient with 36 color stops. Useful for detailed gradients.

_64.en: Generates a gradient with 64 color stops. Produces a very smooth color lookup.

_128.en: Generates a gradient with 128 color stops. Ideal for high-fidelity color transitions.

_256.en: Generates a gradient with 256 color stops. Recommended for ultra-smooth gradients.

_1024.en: Generates a gradient with 1024 color stops. Used for extremely fine color detail.

_2048.en: Generates a gradient with 2048 color stops. Maximum smoothness for professional-grade color lookup.

Fuzzy.en: Controls the amount of fuzziness or blur applied to the gradient, affecting the softness of color transitions in the bitmap image.

Offset.en: Shifts the position of the gradient along its axis, allowing adjustment of where color stops are mapped.

Seed.en: Defines the randomization pattern or seed for the node's process, ensuring reproducible results when generating gradients.

Synthesize Colors.en: Generates a color lookup gradient based on the specified number of samples and other parameters. The resulting gradient can be used for terrain coloring or other visual effects.

Export JSON.en: Exports the synthesized gradient and node configuration as a JSON file for use in other applications or for documentation purposes.

Terraces.en: Creates stepped terrace formations from the terrain.
Controls the number and spacing of terrace steps applied to the terrain. Increasing this value creates more distinct, layered steps.

Uniformity.en: Adjusts the consistency of terrace step heights. Higher uniformity produces evenly spaced terraces, while lower values introduce variation.

Steepness.en: Sets the vertical sharpness of each terrace step. Higher steepness results in more abrupt transitions between steps.

Intensity.en: Determines the overall strength of the terrace effect. Higher intensity makes the terraces more pronounced in the terrain.

Seed.en: Defines the randomization seed for procedural terrace generation. Changing the seed produces different terrace patterns.

TextureBaker.en: Bakes derived texture maps from the terrain for export and downstream use.

Generate Normals.en: Enables the generation of tangent-space normal maps for the mesh. When checked, MeshWarp will output normal maps that align with the mesh geometry at each LOD, suitable for advanced shading and detail.

Add Input.en: Adds an additional input port to connect masks, color maps, or other data layers. Each input will be processed and fitted to the mesh at all LODs.

LOD Info.en: Shows Level of Detail (LOD) information for the mesh and all connected maps. Each input map will have an LOD generated to match the mesh's LODs as set in the Mesher node.

TextureBase.en: Texture uses multiple factors (such as chaos, slopes, flow zones, and other geological features) to create a texture mask for any color node to create a texture map. Can be used by itself, or combined with other data maps and selectors.

Structure.en: Controls the influence of terrain slope on the texture, allowing highlights or patterns to follow steeper areas.

Slope.en: Controls the influence of terrain slope on the texture, allowing highlights or patterns to follow steeper areas.

Flows.en: Adds flow-based features to the texture, simulating the effect of water or material movement across the surface.

Soil.en: Introduces soil-like patterns or noise, adding organic variation to the texture.

Patches.en: Controls the presence and size of patchy areas within the texture, creating irregular or clustered features.

Chaos.en: Adjusts the randomness and disorder in the texture, increasing natural variation and reducing uniformity.

Peaks.en: Emphasizes or introduces features that follow terrain peaks, adding detail to high areas in the texture.

Processing.en: Enhances specific features or contrasts in the texture, making details more pronounced.

Accentuate.en: Enhances specific features or contrasts in the texture, making details more pronounced.

Off.en: No accentuation is applied; the texture remains unmodified.

Old.en: Applies the legacy accentuation method, increasing contrast and detail using the previous algorithm.

New.en: Uses the latest accentuation method for improved feature enhancement and clarity.

Enhance.en: Applies additional enhancement to the texture's tonal range or contrast.

None.en: No enhancement is applied.

Autolevel.en: Automatically adjusts the levels to maximize the full tonal range, improving contrast.

Equalize.en: Equalizes the histogram, distributing intensity values more evenly for a balanced look.

Reverse.en: Inverts the black and white values of the texture, swapping dark and light areas.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating the texture. Changing the seed produces different pattern variations.

Texturizer.en: Generates terrain texture masks using preset styles and controllable secondary effects.

Style.en: Select from A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, or L. Each option represents a distinct pre-defined texture style, allowing you to experiment and choose the look that best fits your terrain.

Factor.en: Primary driver controlling the overall strength or intensity of the selected style. Higher values increase the prominence of the texture effect.

Secondary.en: Adjusts the strength of secondary effects such as soil accumulation, flow streaks, and breakup patterns. Use to fine-tune the complexity and realism of the texture.

Seed.en: Randomizes the pattern while keeping other settings the same, allowing for variation without the need to re-tune parameters.

Components.en: Simulates natural erosion channels and directional streaks, adding realism by mimicking the effects of water or wind movement across the terrain.

Flows.en: Simulates natural erosion channels and directional streaks, adding realism by mimicking the effects of water or wind movement across the terrain.

Slope.en: Adds slope-based weighting to the texture, favoring either steeper or flatter areas to enhance natural variation.

Soil.en: Controls soil-like accumulation in flatter regions, adding natural buildup and enhancing the realism of the terrain surface.

Thermal.en: Thermal simulates Thermal Erosion to create talus and debris.
Thermal.zh: 模拟热力侵蚀，生成岩屑坡（talus）与碎屑堆积。

Erosion.en: Controls how long the thermal erosion process is applied. Higher values result in more extensive terrain changes over time.
Erosion.zh: 热力侵蚀作用时长。越高变化越明显。

Duration.en: Controls how long the thermal erosion process is applied. Higher values result in more extensive terrain changes over time.
Duration.zh: 热力侵蚀作用时长。越高变化越明显。

Strength.en: Sets the intensity of thermal erosion. Increasing this value produces more pronounced smoothing and displacement, especially on steep slopes.

Anisotropy.en: Adjusts the directional bias of erosion and deposit formation. Low values preserve the original terrain, while high values intensify directional erosion, shaping talus deposits and terrain features.
Anisotropy.zh: 侵蚀与沉积的方向性偏差。

Seed.en: Randomizes the erosion pattern while keeping other settings unchanged, allowing for varied results without retuning parameters.

Talus.en: Sets the maximum slope angle before material begins to move downward, forming talus. Lower angles create gentler slopes, while higher angles allow steeper terrain before shifting occurs.
Talus.zh: 物质开始下滑形成岩屑坡的最大坡角。

Angle.en: Sets the maximum slope angle before material begins to move downward, forming talus. Lower angles create gentler slopes, while higher angles allow steeper terrain before shifting occurs.

Settling.en: Controls how quickly and thoroughly loose material settles after being eroded. Higher values result in faster, more complete settling, while lower values allow for gradual accumulation.

Sediment Removal.en: Determines the amount of sediment removed during talus formation. Higher values produce cleaner, sharper features, while lower values allow more sediment to accumulate, creating smoother transitions.

Scale.en: Sets the scale of the largest thermal erosion features in the terrain. Larger values create broader, more pronounced features; smaller values result in finer details.

Feature Scale.en: Sets the scale of the largest thermal erosion features in the terrain. Larger values create broader, more pronounced features; smaller values result in finer details.

Real Scale.en: Uses the scale defined by the terrain's physical dimensions. Disable to access additional options and manually adjust erosion physics.

Terrain Scale.en: Specifies the overall scale of the terrain when Real Scale is turned off, allowing for manual adjustment of terrain size.

Verticality.en: Controls the height of the terrain when Real Scale is turned off, enabling further customization of vertical exaggeration.

Thermal2.en: Thermal2 is an evolution of the previous node. It creates Thermal Erosion to create realistic talus and debris.

Erosion.en: Controls the duration of the thermal erosion process. Higher values extend the erosion period, resulting in more significant changes to the terrain.

Duration.en: Controls the duration of the thermal erosion process. Higher values extend the erosion period, resulting in more significant changes to the terrain.

Strength.en: Determines the intensity of thermal erosion. Increasing this value produces more pronounced smoothing and displacement of materials, especially on steeper slopes.

Anisotropy.en: Governs the directional bias of erosion and rock deposits. Low values preserve the original terrain with minimal smoothing, while high values intensify erosion, especially on sharp peaks, leading to stronger talus formation and more heavily eroded terrain. Useful for simulating environments with directional erosion influences such as wind or gravity.

Talus.en: Sets the maximum slope angle before materials begin to move downward, forming talus. Lower angles create more gradual slopes, while higher angles allow steeper terrain before material shifts.

Angle.en: Sets the maximum slope angle before materials begin to move downward, forming talus. Lower angles create more gradual slopes, while higher angles allow steeper terrain before material shifts.

Sediment Removal.en: Controls the amount of sediment removed during talus formation. Higher values produce cleaner, sharper features by removing excess material, while lower values allow more sediment to accumulate, resulting in smoother transitions.

Scale.en: Adjusts the scale of thermal erosion features in meters. Larger values create broader, more pronounced features, while smaller values result in finer details.

Feature Scale.en: Adjusts the scale of thermal erosion features in meters. Larger values create broader, more pronounced features, while smaller values result in finer details.
