ThermalShaper.en: ThermalShaper is a fast, basic simulation of the concavity and convexity that can be achieved from thermal erosion. The effect can be exaggerated for artistic effect.

Influence.en: Controls the overall strength of the thermal shaping effect applied to the input terrain. Higher values increase the impact, blending more of the thermal shaping with the original terrain. Mid-range values provide a balance between the effect and the source terrain.

Shape.en: Adjusts the shaping style of the terrain. Negative values condense the terrain into sharp, concise ridges, while positive values bulk up the terrain, creating softer, more rounded features.

Scale.en: Sets the scale at which the thermal shaping is applied. Lower values focus the effect on smaller details and individual ridges, while higher values apply the shaping to larger terrain features, affecting broader mountain ranges.

Microdetail Preservation.en: Preserves fine details from the original terrain during thermal shaping. Higher values maintain more microdetail, such as rocky textures and small features, while lower values result in smoother, more uniform terrain.

Threshold.en: Abs can modify the terrain or mask it by eliminating values higher or lower than the exact value specified.

Level.en: Specifies the threshold value used to separate terrain features. Values above this level are retained, while values below are discarded or set to a minimum. Adjusting the level controls the cutoff point for terrain masking or feature isolation.

TileInput.en: Reads a set of tiles for 1:1 input into a tiled build, or combines it into a single input.

Tint.en: QuickColor quickly maps a 2-color gradient to any mask. Useful for simple scenarios where CLUTer would be overkill.

Start.en: Specifies the starting color of the gradient, mapped to the darkest (black) areas of the input map.

End.en: Specifies the ending color of the gradient, mapped to the brightest (white) areas of the input map.

Hue.en: Adjusts the hue of the gradient colors, allowing for global color shifts across the entire gradient.

Saturation.en: Controls the intensity or vividness of the gradient colors. Higher values produce more vibrant colors, while lower values result in muted tones.

Lightness.en: Sets the overall brightness of the gradient colors, making the output lighter or darker.

Processing.en: Applies additional enhancement to the gradient's tonal range or contrast before tinting.

Enhance.en: Applies additional enhancement to the gradient's tonal range or contrast before tinting.

None.en: No enhancement is applied; the gradient is mapped directly from the input.

Autolevel.en: Automatically adjusts the levels to maximize the full tonal range, improving contrast in the gradient mapping.

Equalize.en: Equalizes the histogram, distributing intensity values more evenly for a balanced gradient effect.

Reverse.en: Inverts the gradient mapping, swapping the start and end colors so that black maps to the end color and white maps to the start color.

Transform.en: Transform moves, rotates, and scales any terrain. A post-process effect, it can be implemented at any point in the graph.

Position.en: Shifts the terrain or object horizontally along the X axis, allowing precise placement within the scene.

Offset X.en: Shifts the terrain or object horizontally along the X axis, allowing precise placement within the scene.

Offset Y.en: Shifts the terrain or object horizontally along the Y axis, moving it forward or backward in the workspace.

Offset Z.en: Moves the terrain or object vertically along the Z axis, raising or lowering its elevation.

Scale.en: Applies uniform scaling to all axes, maintaining the original proportions of the terrain or object.

Uniform.en: Applies uniform scaling to all axes, maintaining the original proportions of the terrain or object.

Scale X.en: The non-uniform scale on the X axis, allowing independent horizontal stretching or compression.

Scale Y.en: The non-uniform scale on the Y axis, allowing independent vertical stretching or compression.

Rotation.en: The angle of rotation applied to the terrain or object, measured in degrees.

Angle.en: The angle of rotation applied to the terrain or object, measured in degrees.

Settings.en: Specifies how the transformed terrain or object is merged with the underlying data or input.

Blend Mode.en: Specifies how the transformed terrain or object is merged with the underlying data or input.

None.en: No blending is applied; the transformed data overwrites the input.

Blend.en: Blends the transformed data with the input using standard alpha or linear blending.

Add.en: Adds the transformed values to the input, increasing elevation or intensity.

Subtract.en: Subtracts the transformed values from the input, creating depressions or reductions.

Difference.en: Emphasizes the difference between the transformed data and the input.

Multiply.en: Multiplies the transformed data with the input, modulating the result.

Screen.en: Uses a screen blend, lightening the result where both inputs are present.

Max.en: Takes the maximum value between the transformed data and the input at each point.

Min.en: Takes the minimum value between the transformed data and the input at each point.

Edges.en: Specifies how the edges of the transformed terrain or object are handled.

None.en: No special edge handling; edges may be abrupt or unblended.

Thin.en: Applies a thin edge blend, softening the transition at the boundaries.

Wide.en: Applies a wide edge blend, creating a broader transition zone at the boundaries.

Soft.en: Applies a soft, gradual edge blend for smooth transitions.

Quality.en: Sets the processing quality for the transform operation.

Draft.en: Fastest processing with lower quality, suitable for previews.

Medium.en: Balanced quality and performance for general use.

High.en: Highest quality with the most detail, recommended for final output.

Transform3D.en: Applies full 3D transformation to the terrain, including rotation and spatial adjustment.

Position.en: Automatically positions the object so its lowest point rests on the ground plane, preventing it from floating or being embedded below the surface.

Drop to Floor.en: Automatically positions the object so its lowest point rests on the ground plane, preventing it from floating or being embedded below the surface.

Offset X.en: Shifts the object horizontally along the X axis, allowing precise placement within the 3D space.

Offset Y.en: Shifts the object horizontally along the Y axis, moving it forward or backward in the 3D scene.

Offset Z.en: Moves the object vertically along the Z axis, raising or lowering its elevation relative to the ground.

Scale.en: Group containing parameters for scaling the object or mesh, affecting its size and proportions in 3D space.

Rotation.en: Rotates the object around the X axis, tilting it forward or backward.

Pitch.en: Rotates the object around the X axis, tilting it forward or backward.

Yaw.en: Rotates the object around the Y axis, turning it left or right.

Roll.en: Rotates the object around the Z axis, spinning it clockwise or counterclockwise.

Quality.en: Enables or adjusts antialiasing for the 3D transformation, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Antialiasing.en: Enables or adjusts antialiasing for the 3D transformation, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Transpose.en: Adapts the terrain to the substructures of a given reference terrain.

Mode.en: Specifies the method used to transpose or rearrange the input data. Each mode determines how the transformation is applied.

Transpose.en: Swaps the X and Y axes of the input, effectively rotating the terrain or image by 90 degrees.

Embed.en: Inserts the transposed data into a larger canvas or area, preserving the original orientation within a new context.

Insert.en: Places the transposed data into a specific position within the output, allowing for targeted rearrangement.

Amount.en: Controls the degree or strength of the transposition effect, allowing for partial or full transformation.

Extend.en: Determines whether the output is extended to accommodate the transposed data, preventing cropping or loss of information.

Flatten.en: Flattens the result after transposition, removing any elevation or depth variations if enabled.

Threshold.en: Sets a cutoff value for the transposition effect, limiting the transformation to areas above or below the specified threshold.

Boundary.en: Defines how the edges or boundaries are handled during transposition, such as wrapping, clamping, or mirroring.

Trees.en: The Arboreal Node gives you the power of creating superficial forests and vegetation. These forests are part of the heightfield while being "detached" enough for various export scenarios.

Determines the output type for tree placement. 'Instances' provides individual tree positions for rendering and export. 'AreaMask' is an experimental feature that outputs a mask of tree coverage, useful for blending or exclusion but may be less reliable.

Output.en: Determines the output type for tree placement. 'Instances' provides individual tree positions for rendering and export. 'AreaMask' is an experimental feature that outputs a mask of tree coverage, useful for blending or exclusion but may be less reliable.

Instances.en: Outputs individual tree instance data for use in rendering, simulation, or export. Recommended for stable and reliable results.

AreaMask.en: Outputs a mask indicating areas where trees are placed. Useful for visualization and blending, but currently experimental and may produce less predictable results.

Count in Thousands.en: Sets the number of trees to be placed, specified in thousands. Higher values increase density and mask quality but may impact performance and memory usage.

Is Relative.en: If enabled, tree count scales with terrain resolution for consistent density. Recommended for predictable results at higher resolutions, but may increase resource usage.

LOD Info.en: Provides Level of Detail (LOD) information for tree instances, enabling optimized rendering and export at different distances or resolutions.

Tree Size.en: Controls the height of each tree instance. Affects the appearance of exported trees but not the mask. Useful for adjusting the final look of tree outputs.

Trim Under.en: Removes tree instances below a certain size threshold, clamping down on smaller or weaker trees to refine the mask and output.

Shape.en: Specifies the distribution pattern or type of tree shapes. 'Point' is a single pixel, 'Big' is a larger square, and 'BigOnly' restricts placement to large clusters. 'Big' is preferred for mask export, while 'Point' is better for visualization.

Point.en: Places trees as single small pixels, resulting in sparse and detailed distribution. Best for internal visualization.

Big.en: Places larger tree shapes, creating denser and more legible masks. Preferred for exporting tree masks.

BigOnly.en: Restricts placement to only large tree clusters, excluding smaller or individual trees for a bold mask.

Seed.en: Sets the randomization seed for procedural tree placement. Changing the seed produces different tree layouts and simulation results.

Growth.en: Controls whether trees grow near water flows ('Seek') or away from them ('Avoid'). Useful for simulating species preferences and biomes.

Seek Water.en: Controls whether trees grow near water flows ('Seek') or away from them ('Avoid'). Useful for simulating species preferences and biomes.

Seek.en: Trees preferentially grow near water sources and flow areas, simulating water-loving species.

Avoid.en: Trees avoid water sources and flow areas, simulating species that prefer drier conditions.

Avoid Trees.en: Masks out areas occupied by other tree nodes, useful for stacking multiple tree species or biomes without overlap.

None.en: No avoidance; trees can be placed close together or overlap with other tree nodes.

Previous.en: New trees avoid areas occupied by the previously placed tree node, reducing overlap in stacked nodes.

All.en: New trees avoid all other tree nodes in the stack, maximizing spacing and separation.

Health.en: Controls the duration and vigor of the tree simulation. Higher health increases density and allows trees to grow into smaller valleys and more challenging terrain. Lower health restricts growth to main flow areas.

Patches.en: Clumps trees together into larger groups, creating stylized patches instead of individual trees. Useful for natural-looking forests.

Spread.en: Blurs and expands the area where trees can grow, merging small flows into larger masses and creating more natural, contiguous forest areas.

Random.en: Adds random noise to tree placement, scattering trees across the terrain without regard to inhibition or aspect controls. Rarely used for realistic masks.

Aspect Inhibition.en: Restricts tree growth on steep terrain. Not recommended when using a custom inhibition mask, as the mask provides more accurate control.

Slope.en: Restricts tree growth on steep terrain. Not recommended when using a custom inhibition mask, as the mask provides more accurate control.

Slope Falloff.en: Controls how quickly tree density decreases as slope increases. Use with slope inhibition for gradual or sharp transitions.

Altitude.en: Sets altitude limits for tree placement, simulating elevation-based growth restrictions. Works well with both aspect inhibition and custom masks.

Altitude Falloff.en: Controls the rate at which tree density decreases with altitude, enabling smooth or sharp transitions in elevation-based inhibition.

Peaks.en: Removes tree growth from exposed mountain peaks, preventing trees from growing in the most exposed areas.

Strict.en: Enforces strict adherence to inhibition rules, resulting in sharper falloff and less natural tree distribution. Use for precise, non-organic masks.

Snow Inhibition.en: Represents areas where tree growth is suppressed due to snow mass or adverse conditions. Controls the amount of snow mass moving down the terrain.

Dead Flow.en: Represents areas where tree growth is suppressed due to snow mass or adverse conditions. Controls the amount of snow mass moving down the terrain.

Consolidate Flows.en: Groups snow flows into larger masses, affecting how far snow moves down the terrain and influencing tree inhibition.

Bias.en: Directs snow flows to move less or more, affecting the inhibition of tree growth in snowy areas.

Snowline.en: Defines the altitude at which snow flows start, restricting tree growth above this line.

Artistic Control.en: Warps tree positions for a more natural, randomized look, breaking up straight flows and adding organic variation.

Chaos.en: Warps tree positions for a more natural, randomized look, breaking up straight flows and adding organic variation.

Blur Edges.en: Softens and tapers the edges of tree patches, blending them into the terrain for a more natural transition.

Visualize Data.en: Enables visualization of tree placement, flows, and snow inhibition, assisting with mask tuning and debugging.

Custom Inhibitors.en: Applies custom influence maps or masks to control tree placement according to user specifications, enabling highly tailored results.

Custom Influence.en: Applies custom influence maps or masks to control tree placement according to user specifications, enabling highly tailored results.

Trim.en: Removes trees from specified areas, allowing for manual or procedural clearing of tree patches for refined mask output.

Unity.en: Exports terrain data in Unity-friendly resolutions and formats.

Target Size.en: Specifies the export resolution for Unity terrain heightmaps and textures. Select from standard Unity-compatible sizes to ensure proper import and terrain fidelity.

x8193.en: Exports at 8193 x 8193 pixels, suitable for very large Unity terrains requiring maximum detail.

x4097.en: Exports at 4097 x 4097 pixels, commonly used for large terrain tiles in Unity.

x2049.en: Exports at 2049 x 2049 pixels, ideal for medium-sized Unity terrain tiles.

x1025.en: Exports at 1025 x 1025 pixels, suitable for smaller terrain tiles or test scenes in Unity.

x513.en: Exports at 513 x 513 pixels, used for small terrain tiles or prototyping in Unity.

Add Input.en: Adds an additional input map layer for export, allowing for more complex terrain data to be sent to Unity.

Unreal.en: Exports terrain data in Unreal-friendly resolutions, formats, and naming conventions.

Automatic Size.en: Automatically determines the optimal export resolution for Unreal Engine based on the input terrain and project settings.

Target Size.en: Specifies the desired export resolution for Unreal Engine heightmaps and textures. Choose from standard Unreal-compatible sizes for best results.

x8129.en: Exports at 8129 x 8129 pixels, suitable for very large landscapes in Unreal Engine.

x4033.en: Exports at 4033 x 4033 pixels, commonly used for large terrain tiles.

x2017.en: Exports at 2017 x 2017 pixels, ideal for medium-sized terrain tiles.

x1009.en: Exports at 1009 x 1009 pixels, suitable for smaller terrain tiles or test scenes.

x505.en: Exports at 505 x 505 pixels, used for small terrain tiles or prototyping.

Dont Resize Textures.en: Prevents automatic resizing of textures during export, preserving the original resolution of input textures.

LOD Info.en: Provides Level of Detail (LOD) information for exported terrain, enabling optimized rendering and streaming in Unreal Engine.

Format.en: Selects the file format for exported terrain data. Choose the format that best matches your Unreal Engine workflow.

PNG.en: Exports terrain data as PNG images, suitable for color maps and masks.

R16.en: Exports terrain data as 16-bit RAW files, recommended for heightmaps to preserve elevation detail.

RAW.en: Exports terrain data as RAW files, compatible with Unreal Engine for heightmaps and other data.

Naming.en: Applies Unreal Engine-compatible naming conventions to exported files for easier import and organization.

Unreal Friendly Naming.en: Applies Unreal Engine-compatible naming conventions to exported files for easier import and organization.

Add Input.en: Adds an additional input map layer for export, allowing for more complex terrain data to be sent to Unreal Engine.

Information.en: Additional metadata or notes related to the Unreal Engine export process.

Information 2.en: Additional metadata or notes related to the Unreal Engine export process.

Uplift.en: Creates tectonic-style uplift by raising and shaping large terrain masses.

Var.en: Reads or modifies named graph variables for procedural control and automation.

Edit Mode.en: Specifies how the variable is used in the node. 'Consume' reads the value of an existing variable, while 'Modify' changes the value or applies an expression to the variable.

Consume.en: Reads and uses the value of the specified variable without altering it.

Modify.en: Applies an expression or new value to the variable, updating its value for subsequent nodes.

Variable Name.en: The name of the variable to consume or modify. This should match the variable defined elsewhere in the graph or macro.

Expression.en: An optional mathematical or logical expression to apply when modifying the variable. Used only in 'Modify' mode.

Default Value.en: The value to use if the specified variable is not set or available. Ensures the node has a fallback value.

VariableBlur.en: Blurs the input by varying the blur amount across the surface using local data or a guide.

Blur.en: Controls the blur radius for each pixel. The radius can vary across the image, enabling localized or mask-driven blur effects.

Radius.en: Controls the blur radius for each pixel. The radius can vary across the image, enabling localized or mask-driven blur effects.

Volcano.en: Generates a volcanic landform with a central cone and crater structure.

Scale.en: Controls the overall size of the volcano feature in the terrain. Increasing the scale makes the volcano larger relative to the surrounding landscape.

Height.en: Sets the maximum elevation of the volcano. Higher values produce taller volcanic structures.

Mouth.en: Defines the diameter of the volcano's crater opening. Adjusting this parameter changes how wide or narrow the mouth appears.

Bulk.en: Determines the mass and thickness of the volcano's body. Higher bulk values result in a more massive and robust volcano shape.

Surface.en: Specifies the surface characteristics of the volcano, allowing selection between different terrain styles for the outer slopes.

Smooth.en: Applies a smooth surface to the volcano, minimizing roughness and erosion effects for a clean, uniform appearance.

Eroded.en: Applies erosion effects to the volcano's surface, simulating weathered and worn terrain with more natural detail.

X.en: Sets the horizontal position of the volcano on the terrain grid. Adjust to move the volcano left or right.

Y.en: Sets the vertical position of the volcano on the terrain grid. Adjust to move the volcano up or down.

Seed.en: Defines the randomization seed for procedural generation. Changing the seed produces different volcano shapes and features.

Voronoi.en: Voronoi is a staple of procedural design and creates sharp, geometric patterns. In Gaea, we've made a "geo-variant" by modifying the base Voronoi shape to fit the needs of terrain design from the beginning.

Noise.en: The perceptual scale of the Voronoi shapes. Higher values create more, smaller shapes; lower values produce fewer, larger cells.

Scale.en: The perceptual scale of the Voronoi shapes. Higher values create more, smaller shapes; lower values produce fewer, larger cells.

Jitter.en: Controls the offset of the Voronoi points, ranging from perfectly symmetrical (low jitter) to highly chaotic (high jitter) cell placement.

Function.en: Specifies the distance function used to calculate Voronoi cells, affecting the shape and boundaries of each cell.

Euclidean.en: Uses the standard Euclidean distance, resulting in natural, rounded cell shapes.

Manhattan.en: Uses the Manhattan (grid-based) distance, producing square or diamond-shaped cells.

Form.en: Determines how the height or value of each Voronoi cell is calculated, affecting the resulting terrain or pattern.

C.en: Voronoi cells with height determined by the cell itself, creating classic cell-based patterns.

N.en: Voronoi cells with height determined by the nearest neighbor, resulting in smoother transitions between cells.

R.en: Voronoi cells with height influenced by the distance to the cell's edge, creating ring-like or ridge effects.

P.en: The default look for this geo-variant, suitable for creating mountainous terrain with prominent peaks.

A.en: A mix between the P and M forms, blending characteristics of both for varied terrain features.

S.en: Generates individual mountains with fully separated boundaries, emphasizing isolated peaks.

M.en: Favors the strongest cell, ideal for creating a large mountain slope or dominant landform.

D.en: Emphasizes ridges over cell centers, producing terrain with pronounced ridge lines.

Gain.en: Adjusts the contrast or intensity of the Voronoi pattern, amplifying or reducing the difference between cell heights.

Clamp.en: Limits the output values to a specified range, preventing extreme heights or depths in the generated pattern.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different Voronoi arrangements.

Warp.en: Specifies the type of warp applied to the Voronoi pattern, controlling the complexity of the distortion.

Type.en: Specifies the type of warp applied to the Voronoi pattern, controlling the complexity of the distortion.

None.en: No warping is applied; the Voronoi pattern remains unaltered.

Simple.en: Applies basic warping to the pattern, introducing gentle distortions.

Complex.en: Applies advanced, multi-layered warping for highly intricate and organic distortions.

Frequency.en: Controls the frequency of the warp, determining how often the pattern is distorted across the terrain.

Amplitude.en: Sets the strength of the warp effect, controlling how far the Voronoi cells are displaced.

Octaves.en: Specifies the number of detail layers used in the warp, increasing the complexity and richness of the distortion.

Transform.en: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the pattern horizontally.

Scale X.en: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the pattern horizontally.

Scale Y.en: The non-uniform scale of the Y axis, stretching or compressing the pattern vertically.

X.en: Offsets the Voronoi pattern along the X axis, shifting its position horizontally.

Y.en: Offsets the Voronoi pattern along the Y axis, shifting its position vertically.

Warp.en: Warp can take the terrain and "warp" the shape creating more believable shapes or alter simple shapes into a more complex formation. It can help breakup masks too.
The size of the warp noise. Controls the scale of the distortion pattern applied to the input.

Size.en: The size of the warp noise. Controls the scale of the distortion pattern applied to the input.

Strength.en: The strength of the warp noise. Higher values produce more pronounced distortions.

Z Scale.en: Vertical axis scale for the noise, affecting the intensity of the warp along the Z (height) axis.

Warp Source.en: Selects the noise or pattern used as the source for the warp. Choose from built-in options or provide a custom source.

PerlinFBM.en: Uses Perlin fractal Brownian motion noise as the warp source, producing smooth, natural distortions.

VoronoiR.en: Uses Voronoi (R) noise as the warp source, creating cell-like, ridged distortions.

VoronoiP.en: Uses Voronoi (P) noise as the warp source, suitable for generating mountainous or peak-like distortions.

VoronoiA.en: Uses Voronoi (A) noise as the warp source, blending characteristics of other Voronoi types for varied effects.

VoronoiS.en: Uses Voronoi (S) noise as the warp source, emphasizing separated, individual cell boundaries.

VoronoiM.en: Uses Voronoi (M) noise as the warp source, favoring dominant cells for strong, directional warping.

VoronoiD.en: Uses Voronoi (D) noise as the warp source, emphasizing ridges and linear features in the distortion.

Perturbation.en: Applies additional random displacement to the warp, increasing the irregularity and complexity of the effect.

Complexity.en: The complexity of the warp noise source. Higher values add more detail and layers to the distortion.

Roughness.en: The roughness of the warp noise. Higher values (especially above 0.5) create harsher, more jagged distortions.

Normalized.en: Specifies whether the noise is normalized. Normalization ensures the output remains within a standard range.

Edge Behaviour.en: Determines how the warp handles the edges of the input, preventing visible seams or artifacts.

Edge.en: Applies standard edge handling, which may result in wrapping or stretching at the borders.

Mirror.en: Edge pixels are mirrored, creating seamless, reflected borders for the warp effect.

Modulation.en: The amount of modulation to use from the Modulation input (if connected), allowing external control over the warp intensity.

Modulation Direction.en: Sets the direction of the modulation, controlling how the modulation input influences the warp.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different warp results.

Iterative.en: Number of warp iterations to apply. More iterations increase the complexity and layering of the distortion.

Iterations.en: Number of warp iterations to apply. More iterations increase the complexity and layering of the distortion.

Mode.en: Specifies the mode used for iterative warping, affecting how each pass is calculated and applied.

Bitmap.en: Applies the warp using standard bitmap-based processing for each iteration.

VectorField.en: Uses a vector field to guide the warp, allowing for more directional and flow-based distortions.

VectorFieldIntegral.en: Integrates the vector field over multiple passes, producing complex, cumulative warp effects.

WaterColor.en: Colorizes water bodies using palette-based shallow and deep water tones.

WaveShine.en: Generates wave-like reflective or rippling patterns useful for stylized surfaces and water-like forms.

Global.en: Specifies the current animation frame or time step for the wave simulation, allowing for frame-by-frame control or preview.

Frame.en: Specifies the current animation frame or time step for the wave simulation, allowing for frame-by-frame control or preview.

Octaves.en: Sets the number of detail layers (octaves) used in the wave pattern, increasing complexity and realism with higher values.

Seed.en: Randomization seed for generating unique wave patterns. Changing the seed produces different wave arrangements.

Ripples.en: Controls the speed at which ripples animate across the surface, affecting how quickly the pattern evolves over time.

Animation Speed.en: Controls the speed at which ripples animate across the surface, affecting how quickly the pattern evolves over time.

Size.en: Sets the scale of individual ripples, with larger values producing broader, more widely spaced ripples.

Amplitude.en: Adjusts the height or intensity of the ripples, making them more or less pronounced.

Direction.en: Specifies the primary direction in which ripples travel, simulating wind or current-driven movement.

Speed.en: Controls the movement speed of the ripples, determining how fast they propagate across the surface.

Wind Patch.en: Sets the strength of the wind patch effect, increasing the impact of wind on the wave or ripple pattern.

Intensity.en: Sets the strength of the wind patch effect, increasing the impact of wind on the wave or ripple pattern.

Contrast.en: Adjusts the contrast of the wind patch effect, making the difference between calm and windy areas more or less pronounced.

Lighting.en: Controls the overall brightness of the rendered wave surface, affecting how light or dark the result appears.

Brightness.en: Controls the overall brightness of the rendered wave surface, affecting how light or dark the result appears.

Sun Azimuth.en: Sets the horizontal angle of the sun, determining the direction of sunlight and resulting highlights or reflections.

Sun Elevation.en: Sets the vertical angle of the sun above the horizon, affecting the length and intensity of highlights and shadows on the waves.

Weathering.en: Creates weathered color or mask variation that simulates dirt, fading, and environmental wear.

Primary.en: Sets the scale at which weathering effects are applied. Lower values target fine details, while higher values affect larger terrain features.

Scale.en: Sets the scale at which weathering effects are applied. Lower values target fine details, while higher values affect larger terrain features.

Creep.en: Simulates gradual movement and spreading of weathering effects across the terrain, softening transitions and blending weathered areas.

Amount.en: Adjusts the overall intensity of the weathering effect. Higher values produce more pronounced weathering.

Washed Out.en: Toggles if colors are faded or desaturated, mimicking the effect of prolonged exposure to the elements.

Inverse.en: Inverts the weathering effect, applying it to areas that would normally be less affected, such as recesses instead of protrusions.

Dirt.en: Adds darker coloration to crevices, nooks, and sheltered areas of the terrain, simulating the accumulation of soil, organic matter, or moisture.

Darker.en: Intensifies the darkness of the dirt effect, making crevices and nooks appear deeper and more shadowed.

Post Processing.en: Adjusts the overall hue of the weathered terrain, allowing for color shifts to match desired environmental conditions.

Hue.en: Adjusts the overall hue of the weathered terrain, allowing for color shifts to match desired environmental conditions.

Saturation.en: Controls the intensity of colors in the weathered terrain, from muted to vibrant.

Lightness.en: Sets the overall brightness of the weathered terrain, affecting how light or dark the final result appears.

Whorl.en: Whorl applies multiple vortex-like distortions across the terrain to create large-scale warping. Very useful for creating massive landscapes without a patterning in the noise and for creating slightly surreal or alien landscapes.

Stretch.en: Whorls appear as stretched, interconnected formations.

Spin.en: Whorls appear as round, independent formations.

Whorls.en: The number of whorls to add to the terrain.

Power.en: The strength of the distortion applied with each whorl.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Wizard.en: The Erosion Wizard is a lightweight wrapper for the Erosion node. It simplifies the settings through curated presets, and provides secondary passes for additional processing.

Erosion.en: Sets the strength of fluvial erosion. This parameter controls the sediment transport capacity, that is how much of dissolved minerals water can carry. This parameter can be set to value that is higher than 1.0, this can speed up the erosion process, but also can result in lesser erosion quality, especially if erosion softness value is high too.

Strength.en: Sets the strength of fluvial erosion. This parameter controls the sediment transport capacity, that is how much of dissolved minerals water can carry. This parameter can be set to value that is higher than 1.0, this can speed up the erosion process, but also can result in lesser erosion quality, especially if erosion softness value is high too.

Density.en: Controls the density of rock material. The softer rock is, the faster is erosion process but may produce bulbous deposits.

Material.en: Defines the general material of the terrain, ranging from fine sand to large rocks, or a mix of both.

Channel Depth.en: This parameter controls the amount of downcutting, or vertical erosion. This results in deeper channels, and can be useful for getting mountain ranges.

Channel Width.en: This parameter controls the width of the channels by creating sediment deposits in the base of the channels.

Deposits.en: This controls the amount of sedimentary deposits generated by the erosion process.

Removal.en: This parameter can reduce the amount of sediments generated during erosion, creating deeper channels.

Bulk.en: Increases the bulk of the terrain before eroding. When using strong settings, having some bulk can help prevent the terrain from eroding too much and losing its shape.

Seed.en: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.

Wizard2.en: A simplified erosion wrapper that provides curated controls for shaping erosion depth, scale, and strength.
